courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Elementary French I
courses.description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing in French and to the culture of French-speaking regions.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Elementary French II
courses.description: Continued listening, speaking, reading, and writing in French with further study of the culture of French-speaking regions.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Intermediate French I
courses.description: A rapid review of grammar with continued use of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in French, all with a cultural emphasis.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Intermediate French II
courses.description: This course focuses on listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in French in an introduction to literature and within a cultural context.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Topics of current interest in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Survey of French Literature
courses.description: This course introduces students to French literature. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French Literature from 1800 to 1900
courses.description: Romanticism, the reappearance of lyric poetry, the importance of the individual as opposed to classical anonymity. Realism and naturalism with emphasis on the development of the novel. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French Literature from 1900 to Present
courses.description: Exploration of currents in modern prose, poetry, and drama. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Drama Workshop
courses.description: Literary and theatrical aspects of French drama are explored through class discussion and performance of selections from contemporary and classical plays.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: France Today I
courses.description: Culture, history, and geography of modern France through lectures, videos, downloads from the Internet, audio recordings, digital media, and class discussions. Short papers treating assigned topics to enhance writing skills. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: France Today II
courses.description: Culture, history, and geography of modern France through lectures, videos, audio recordings, digital media, and class discussions. Short papers treating assigned topics to enhance writing skills. Conducted in French.

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Introduction to Contemporary France
courses.description: This course will introduce students to issues in contemporary France. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Social Identities in Contemporary French Culture
courses.description: Analysis of production, reception and perceptions of clashing class identities in France via films, novels, plays, short stories, and newspapers. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Paris: Modernity Today
courses.description: This course explores contemporary Paris and its representations in light of its modern history and culture. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French Phonetics
courses.description: A detailed analysis of the significant features of the French sound system, intonation curves, and graphic representation of individual sounds. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Reading and Translation
courses.description: This course will prepare students for the techniques of rapid reading in French, and give them tools to translate and use texts. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: France: Culture, Economy, Commerce I
courses.description: Advanced Business French, overview of French commerce, communications, publicity, various social milieus, and the work place. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: France: Culture, Economy and Commerce II
courses.description: Advanced Business French. Overview of French commerce, communications, publicity, various social milieus, and the work place. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Comics & Graphic Arts
courses.description: This course studies French comics as a genre and its interrelationships with graphic arts and literature. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French Conversation and Culture
courses.description: This class is designed to help students improve their French speaking skills, and use French at an advanced level. Not for beginners. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Advanced Composition
courses.description: In-depth study of advanced grammar patterns as used in written expressions. Conducted in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Introduction to Africa
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course will use a variety of approaches to study significant aspects of contemporary Africa’s societies, cultures, and representations. Taught in English.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Field Work Abroad
courses.description: This course will focus on theme-based individual projects abroad.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Sustainable Communities in France
courses.description: Examines social, cultural, artistic and environmental dimensions of sustainability and concepts of identity, diversity, social equity and inclusion/exclusion in the French context. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French for the Professions I
courses.description: Study aspects of literature, philosophy, culture, geography, history, business, and industry in France and other Francophone countries in these applied-language courses. Taught in French.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French for Business and Technology I
courses.description: Study of business, technological, and cultural issues, tendencies and patterns of behavior among French-speaking people. Value systems and their manifestations. Part of the French intensive summer language program. Admission by application only.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French for Business and Technology II
courses.description: Business organizations and use of technology in France. Specialized vocabularies of economics, engineering, and computer science. Attention to geographical and anthropological aspects of selected social and political situations. Part of the French intensive summer language program. Admission by application only.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: French for Business and Technology Abroad
courses.description: Two-week seminar in France highlighting business and technology. Field study of technology firms, economic trends, business institutions, and cultural protocols. Journals and papers assigned. Admission by application only.

courses.subject: GRMN
courses.title: Elementary German I
courses.description: An introduction to the German language and the culture of the German-speaking world. Beginning of a survey of basic German grammar and the grammar and the development of the four language skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing German. Some aspects of everyday life in the German-speaking world will also be introduced.

courses.subject: GRMN
courses.title: Elementary German II
courses.description: The second part of an introduction to the German language and the culture of the German-speaking world. Completion of the survey of basic German grammar and further development of the four language skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing German. Aspects of everyday life in the German-speaking world will also be introduced.

courses.description: The continuation of HEBW 1501 or for intermediate-level heritage students in the U.S. who can communicate some in Hebrew, but cannot read or write it for academic purposes. Taught in Hebrew.

courses.subject: HIN
courses.title: Elementary Hindi I
courses.description: This first introductory Hindi course teaches basic grammar and develops listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Taught in Hindi. No native speakers allowed.

courses.subject: HIN
courses.title: Elementary Hindi II
courses.description: A continuation to HIND 1001, this course teaches basic grammar and develops listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Taught in Hindi. No native speakers allowed.

courses.subject: HIN
courses.title: Heritage Hindi I
courses.description: For heritage students in the U.S. who have never studied Hindi formally, but who speak some Hindi.

courses.subject: HIN
courses.title: Intermediate Hindi I
courses.description: Review of basic grammatical concepts: conversational, reading, and writing activities; cultural aspects of the Hindi world.

courses.subject: HIN
courses.title: Heritage Hindi II
courses.description: The continuation of HIN 1501 or for intermediate-level heritage students in the U.S. who can communicate some in Hindi, but cannot read or write it for academic purposes. Taught in Hindi.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Survey of U.S. History I
courses.description: A survey of U.S. History to the post-Civil War period. Colonial settlement, the American Revolution and the Constitution, antebellum expansion, slavery and plantation economy, sectional conflict and Civil War, Reconstruction. Includes study of Georgia history during this period.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Survey of U.S. History II
courses.description: A survey of U.S. History from the post-Civil War period to the present. Topics include American industrialization, two world wars, New Deal, and the Civil Rights movement. Includes study of Georgia history during this period.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Europe Since the Renaissance
courses.description: Social, political, economic, and cultural history of Europe since the Renaissance. Topics include Renaissance; Reformation; political, scientific, and industrial revolutions; nationalism; fascism and communism; decolonization.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Engineering in History
courses.description: Uses historical case studies to examine the relationship between engineers and the larger society in which they function. Often taught jointly with engineering faculty.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: This is Archaeology
courses.description: An accessible introduction to the foundations of archaeology and heritage management, including methods, data, interpretation, ethics, and responsibilities toward varied living communities.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special Topics course.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Early American History
courses.description: North America to 1763, including native cultures, contacts with European colonizers, settlement strategies and patterns, and foundation of American political and economic institutions.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The American Revolution and Constitution
courses.description: The American Revolution as political debate, war, and social upheaval, with attention to the framing and ratification of the Constitution.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of the South to 1865
courses.description: A study of social, political, and economic developments in the South from the colonial period through the Civil War. Includes study of Georgia history during this period.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of the Modern South
courses.description: An examination of social, political, and economic developments from the Reconstruction period to the present. Includes study of Georgia history during this period.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern America: World War II and After
courses.description: Dawning of the atomic age, anticommunism, the Civil Rights Movement, New Frontier and Great Society, Vietnam and the tumultuous 1960s, and end of Cold War.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Sports in America
courses.description: Examines American sport from colonial to contemporary times. Focuses on the rise of organized sports and the influence of race, class, gender, and ethnicity.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Social Issues and Public Policy
courses.description: Draws on sociological theory and research to understand the major economic, social, and cultural issues facing American society today.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Environmental Sociology
courses.description: This course examines theories about how human society impacts the natural world through economic, political, and social systems.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Food and Society
courses.description: Survey of the complex social web of identity, culture, politics, economics, history, and power behind food systems in the U.S. and globally.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Revolutionary Europe: 1789-1914
courses.description: Industrialization and political revolution, the development of political ideologies and labor activism, modern nation-state building, and imperialism from the French Revolution to World War I.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Twentieth Century Europe: 1914 to Present
courses.description: Global war and the Bolshevik Revolution, rise and fall of Mussolini and Hitler, Stalinism, the Holocaust, Cold War, decolonization, and the movement toward European integration.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Islamic Societies
courses.description: Survey of Middle East from pre-Islamic times to Ottoman rule, tracing the development of Islamic society and emphasizing the plurality of culture in the region.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of the Modern Middle East
courses.description: The transformation of the Middle East in the modern era and the relationship of the "East" and "West" in the contemporary world.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Global Health and Society
courses.description: The course critically examines how identity, ethical concerns, socio-political and economic hierarchies, and national and international institutional structures undergird global health and define its trajectories.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Colonial Latin America and the World
courses.description: An exploration of colonial Latin America from the perspective of Global History.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: North American Borderlands
courses.description: Introduction to the history of early Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California in the Spanish Colonial period.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern Latin American History
courses.description: Introduces students to the socioeconomic, political, cultural, and environmental conditions that have shaped life in Latin America from the 1800s to the present.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Traditional Asia and Its Legacy
courses.description: Civilizations of East Asia up to 1850, emphasizing traditional cultures in China and Japan, including religion, science, formation of empires, social life, and commerce.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Asia in the Modern World
courses.description: Civilizations of India, China, and Japan since 1600, emphasizing Western impact and adaptation of these countries' political, economic, and social systems.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Introduction to the History of Disease and Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to the history of disease and medicine since the Renaissance focusing on infectious diseases, the rise of germ theory, and evolution of medical training. Cerdit not allowed for both HTS 2080 and HTS 3087.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The Scientific Revolution
courses.description: A critical approach to the Scientific Revolution, introducing students to primary documents and images from the period and emphasizing interpretive strategies and methods.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Technology and Science in the Industrial Age
courses.description: Surveys major developments in technology and science since 1600 and places them in the broader social context of their times.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Technology and Society
courses.description: Analyzes social conditions that promote or retard technological activity, emphasizing role of business, the state, and scientific and engineering professions, and the emergence of consumerism.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Reel History I: US History through Hollywood Films
courses.description: Students evaluate films as sources for specific historical events by viewing films, reading historical documents, and applying critical analysis to written assignments and class discussions.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Semester in the City: Engaging Communities
courses.description: Explores how urban neighborhoods work focusing on Westside neighborhoods from a variety of perspectives. Students will work with residents in designing a sustainability project.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Games, Computers, and Intelligence
courses.description: This course traces the interrelated histories of the mind and computer over the twentieth century.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sci, Tech & Modern World
courses.description: An introduction to perspectives on how developments in science and technology at once reflect and influence politics and society on a global scale.

courses.description: Interdisciplinary survey based on critical readings of the methods historians and social scientists use to generate knowledge about social life. Students engage in "hands-on" research.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of American Business
courses.description: Evolution of business institutions from colonial period to present, including entrepreneurship, business-government relations, institutional innovation, and twentieth century managerial capitalism.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Economic Institutions
courses.description: Examines links between economic structures-markets, regulatory bodies, and labor relations systems-and the wider structural and cultural context.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: American Environmental History
courses.description: Transformation of the North American environment since 1500, including different notions of nature, romantic responses to wilderness during industrialization, rise of conservation movements, and environmental policy.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: United States Labor History
courses.description: The changing nature of work and labor relations, with focus on unionization and government regulation, and equity issues in the workplace.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Work, Industry, and Occupations
courses.description: Analyzes paid employment as a decisive social attachment, emphasizing work organizations, technological change and authority relations, and social inequality among diverse groups of employees.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Class, Power, and Social Inequality
courses.description: This course examines how social class and the market economy affect inequality and stratification in the U.S., with additional attention to the roles of race and gender.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The American Civil War
courses.description: Social, economic, political, and military aspects of the Civil War, including causes of the war, military campaigns, and long-term consequences.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Organizing for Social Change
courses.description: Students will explore how people organize to amplify their voices, build power, and enact change. They will apply theory and organizing skills to advance change on campus.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The City in American History
courses.description: Examines the historical background of the American city since colonial times, including city planning, urban technology and services, neighborhoods, and race relations.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Urban Sociology
courses.description: Sociological perspectives on the city, urbanization, and problems of community, evolution of cities and problems of urban life in the United States and Third World.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of the Vietnam War
courses.description: Diplomatic, military, and social aspects of America's war in Vietnam, including antiwar protests, the defense industry boom, and the war's enduring impact on American life.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Women and Gender in the United States
courses.description: Course examines themes and theories of women's and gender history since the colonial period, including work, family, race, sexuality, and politics.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Gender
courses.description: Gender as a dimension of social life that shapes and is shaped by the economy, schooling, family, politics, medicine and health, race, and social class.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: New Religions and Cults in America
courses.description: Explores controversial and influential new religious movements and cults in America, focusing on their origin, appeal, and impact.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The Family, Sexuality, and Social Change in America
courses.description: Changing patterns of family life and sex roles since colonial times, with a focus on mainstream ideals, utopian alternatives, and social criticism.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Gender and Technology
courses.description: Course examines the ways in which the design, development, and application of technologies, as well as cultural responses to them, have been gendered historically.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Women in Science and Engineering
courses.description: Women in science and engineering and gender differences in participation, location, and status. Examines education, access, and apprenticeship, culture of science and engineering.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Gender and Sports
courses.description: Examines how gender norms and beliefs shape sport structures, participation opportunities and experiences in American sport.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Slaves without Masters: Free People of Color before 1865
courses.description: Free people of color during the era of slavery, including everyday life, political and social philosophies, literature, community development, and movements for social change.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: African American History to 1865
courses.description: The experience of African and African American people in North America from the beginnings of slavery until the era of emancipation in the Civil War.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: African American History since 1865
courses.description: The African American experience since 1865, including Reconstruction, segregation, the African American family, the Harlem Renaissance, the Civil Rights Movement, and Black Power.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Race and Ethnicity
courses.description: Nature and significance of dominant/minority relations, including legacies of colonialism and slavery, roots of residential segregation, and effects of race on American politics.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The Civil Rights Movement
courses.description: Examines why the civil rights movement emerged, how it was successful, and the impact it had on the U.S.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Ancient Greece: Gods, Heroes, and RuinS
courses.description: Classical Athens and Sparta, myths and legends in historical context. Course ends with Alexander the Great and the rise of Rome.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Ancient Rome: From Greatness to Ruins
courses.description: Growth of the Republic, antics and follies of the emperors, accomplishments of Rome, and causes of decline. Early Christianity and its impact on Europe included.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Medieval Europe: 350 to 1400
courses.description: The rise of barbarian kingdoms from Rome's ashes, the explosion of Islam, the monastic movement, Charlemagne's empire, the blossoming of medieval culture, and developinG European monarchies.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: European Labor History
courses.description: The labor movement from 1700s to the present, including an examination of Marx and socialism, unionization, and work conditions, especially in Britain, Germany, and France.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern European Intellectual History
courses.description: Introduction to intellectual problems and trends in modern Europe, including loss of faith in progress, evil and ethics, post-colonialism, feminism, linguistics, and psycho-analytic thought.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Medieval England
courses.description: Political, economic, and cultural development of England during the Middle Ages (c. 350-1400). Myths and legends of Stonehenge, the Druids, and King Arthur's Camelot explored.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Britain from 1815-1914
courses.description: Developments in nineteenth-century Britain, including the industrial revolution, the growth of political democracy, imperialism, and movements for Irish Home rule and democratic socialism.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Britain Since 1914
courses.description: Britain's experience of two world wars, the growth of Labour and decline of the Liberals, the Welfare State, Thatcherism, and Tony Blair's "New Labour".

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: The French Revolution
courses.description: Economic, intellectual, and cultural causes of the French Revolution, Jacobinism and the Terror, careers of Robespierre and Danton, and rise and fall of Napoleon's empire.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern France
courses.description: France from 1815 to 1968, emphasizing the continuing project of creating France as a powerful nation within the context of global culture and politics.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern Spain
courses.description: Resistance to Napoleon, deformed industrialization, Anarchist and fascist experiments form the background for Spain's transition from dictatorship to democracy after Franco's death.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Science, Politics, and Culture in Nazi Germany
courses.description: Examines the social, political and cultural context of science and technology in Nazi Germany to understand the interaction of science and politics under totalitarian regimes.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern Russian History and Society
courses.description: Provides an overview of Russian history during the 20th Century. Special emphasis will be on the Soviet period of Russian history from 1917-1991.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Women and the Politics of Gender in the Middle East
courses.description: The role of women in imperial, nationalist, and Islamist political programs in the Middle East and the impact of politics on women's lives.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Globalization in the Modern Era
courses.description: This course examines the process of globalization and global change in the twentieth century. Also offers a critical examination of various theories of globalization.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern China
courses.description: The decline of Confucian order, the impact of the West, changes and continuities of Chinese culture, the Communist revolution, nationalism, and economic reforms since 1978.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Modern Japan
courses.description: Japan's transformation in one century from a feudal state into an economic superpower and the impact of these changes on the Japanese people.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Development
courses.description: Course examines competing perspectives on international development and surveys some of the crucial issues, including political instability, facing the Third World today.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Global Societies
courses.description: Examines the historical patterns of interaction and inter- dependence between world regions, from approximately the 13th century to global interdependence to the contemporary world.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Politics and Society
courses.description: Political sociology studies the way power is distributed in society. This course takes a comparative and historical approach, focusing on the development of the nation-state.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Revolutionary Movements in the Modern World
courses.description: Comparative analysis of the origin, development, and impact of major twentieth century revolutionary movements.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Social Movements
courses.description: Why do social movements emerge? Why might they succeed? This course examines how ordinary people challenge powerful segments of society and contribute to social change.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Culture and Society
courses.description: Covers core issues in the study of culture. Focuses on key sites, social practices, and institutions. Topics include education, medicine, consumption, and the mass media.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Crime
courses.description: This course examines the theories and issues such as perceptions of crime and criminals, characteristics of offenders and victims, and how crime is studied.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Education
courses.description: Examines sociological perspectives on how individual, school, and social factors influence students and teachers. Particular attention is paid to gender, race, ethnicity, and social class.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Sports
courses.description: Examines what constitutes "sports," and uses sociological lens to study sports relationship to education, policy, media, deviance, violence as well as gender, race and class.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Foundations of Sports Studies
courses.description: Offers case studies of the multidisciplinary study of sports using the lenses of history, sociology, economics, science and technology to understand sports practices and controversies.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Intelligence and National Security
courses.description: Examines the Cold War’s most important spy cases and operations to better understand the interplay between the world of secrets and intelligence and the world of statecraft and technology.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Rocketry
courses.description: Examines the history of rocketry, scientists, and organizations in the US, USSR, and Europe during the twentieth century.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Technology and the Environment
courses.description: Examines how technology affected the environment during the 20th Century, with special attention to issues like industrialization, pollution, overcrowding, and the biotech revolution.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Science
courses.description: The growth of science, its social structure; deviance and norms, the social context of scientific knowledge and practice, and science policy. Credit not allowed for both HTS 3082 and HTS 6115.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Culture and Technology
courses.description: Modernism and post-modernism: this course investigates culturally creative responses to modern manufacturing, transportation (trains, cars, airplanes), evolving gender ideals, and new communications.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sociology of Medicine and Health
courses.description: Relationship between health and society, including health care problems in the United States and culture's role in defining health and sickness and in determining appropriate therapies.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: History of Medicine
courses.description: An introduction to historical perspectives on the development of medicine, and its relationship to health, illness, and society. Credit not allowed for both HTS 3087 and HTS 2080.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Race, Medicine & Science
courses.description: Examines how race is an issue in medicine and science in ways such as education, professions, treatments, experiments, and as a subject of analysis.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Science, Technology and Sports
courses.description: This course examines what constitutes a "sport," debates on the role of social inequality in sports, and the intersection of science, technology and sport.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Doing Archaeology
courses.description: Hands-on instruction and participation in archaeological methods including research design survey, excavation, documentation, artifact processing, data analysis, preservation, and digital applications in archaeology.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Sharing the Past
courses.description: Explores ethical debates and challenges regarding the role of the past in the present, and the responsibilities of archaeologists and heritage practitioners to varied stakeholders.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
courses.description: Covers theoretical and practical issues in museum studies, including the role of material culture in scholarly work, registration of artifacts, exhibit design, and public relations.

courses.subject: HTS
courses.title: Social Theory and Social Structure
courses.description: Introduction to social theory, providing students with skills for reading theory and examining works of major social theorists, including Marx, Weber, Durkheim, Gilman, and Bourdieu.

courses.description: Surveys the field of global environmental history with examples taken from biology, geography, sociology and anthropology.

courses.description: Examines how science and technology are related to economic institutions and processes. Credit not allowed for both HTS 6118 and HTS 6107.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Human Centered Design
courses.description: This course examines design artifacts in relation to the human body, aging, disabilities, and environments with a perspective of human-centered methodology that includes data gathering, analysis, and usability.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Graduate Studio A
courses.description: Studio introduces the MID certificate in Design. The ID studio class stands at the heart of design education and professional practice. Industrial Design is considered from a strategic perspective. Assignments explore the business, technology and use experience components.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Graduate Studio B
courses.description: This course is a project-based ID studio that gives students an overview of and practice with the insights-driven, iterative ID process.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Rapid Design Vis
courses.description: This course trains students in the basics of sketching and free hand drawing needed in the Industrial Design studio environment.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Brand and Visual Design
courses.description: This course introduces the principles of branding and visual identity. It emphasizes branded experiences in a service/product/mobile context.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: 3D Design Methods
courses.description: This course teaches students about the 3D digital tools needed to develop products for human form. By learning how to model, render and animate, students can better express their research, ideations and designs.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Integrated Product Design
courses.description: Introduction to smart products teaches students to create IOT products. Students work with sensors and signals, U/I design, and multi-platform prototyping.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Survey of Industrial Design History
courses.description: This course surveys the history of industrial design from the Industrial Revolution to contemporary times.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Human Factors and Ergonomics
courses.description: This course teaches students about the human perspective in design, research, and interactions with physical and interface products. Students learn about tools and techniques used instructional design, human-computer interaction, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Graduate Studio One
courses.description: This course introduces the design program philosophy, human-centered design and evidence-driven research from a strategic perspective. Assignments explore the technology, business, and user experience components in the design process and validate the final design with advanced usability tools and methods.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Grad Studio Two: Health and Wellness
courses.description: This course explores the application of systematic product design methods to projects that focus on the design of new and/or improved health products, interactions, and delivery of services.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Grad Studio Two: Interactive Products
courses.description: This course explores the application of systematic product design methods to projects that focus on the design development of new/or improved interactive or smart products.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Service Design, Brand and Value Creation
courses.description: This course introduces students to how data gathering and analysis, perception, visual, product, interface, and service design align to optimize user experiences that drive business service and value creation.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Healthcare Design of the Future
courses.description: Introduction to research-based approaches to integrated healthcare design innovation.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Introduction to Immersive Experiences
courses.description: This course introduces the skills, techniques and software needed to create immersive 3D experiences. These experiences range from augmented reality to virtual reality.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Advance Immersive Experiences
courses.description: This course focuses on teaching the skills, techniques and software needed to create immersive 3D experiences. These experiences will be developed using game engines.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Advance Rendering Techniques
courses.description: This course introduces the skills and techniques needed to create photorealistic renderings. A variety of renderings programs and supporting software will be used.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Master's Project
courses.description: Under the guidance of a faculty member, students explore a design project that relates to advance theoritical research through a human prespective with a design and/or technology focus on a product. The project may include areas in instructional design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Visualizing Interaction
courses.description: Introduction to techniques that empower designers to plan and create effective and clear visual communication depicting the interaction and relationships between people, products, and services.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Intro to Thesis Studies
courses.description: This introduction to thesis course helps students understand the human-centered research methods, analytical tools, and design processes used in developing a thesis or project in graduate studies.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Advanced Sketching
courses.description: This class will focus on developing advanced, traditional (non-digital) sketching, rendering, and presentation techniques.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Parametric Product Modeling
courses.description: This graduate course focuses on advanced digital methods in product modeling for visual analysis, flexible design approaches and digital fabrication methods.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Shape Grammars
courses.description: Shape grammars are a powerful formal system for the generative description, interpretation and evaluation of designs.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Interface Prototyping: Exploring Tools & Theories
courses.description: This course focuses on interface prototypes, how these are used throughout the design process and the varity of ways they can be created with different technologies. Through interface prototypes, students learn how to express their research, receive user feedback, explore user perceptions, and improve their designs.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Crafting Design Methods
courses.description: Traditional craftwork and how we can use material change, scale shifts, methods of manufacture, and algorithmic analysis to incorporate and revitalize these traditions into design.

courses.subject: ID
courses.title: Soft Goods Design
courses.description: This graduate course focuses on product opportunities highlighting user benefits from soft material integration.

courses.subject: ID

courses.description: Preparation for a professional career in HCI. Hands-on workshops in resume and portfolio building, interviewing, public speaking, team work. HCI career choices and trajectories.

courses.description: This course will teach students the fundamentals of web design and usability issues in online environments, with an emphasis on universal design principles and accessibility.

courses.subject: ID

courses.description: This course explores the future of wearable technologies for health by adopting various human-centered design methodologies to meet users’ needs, abilities, and expectations.

courses.description: Final project for students completing a Human-Computer Interaction master's degree in the Digitial Media track. Repeatable for multi-semester projects.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Essentials of Engineering Economy
courses.description: Introduction to engineering economic decision making, economic decision criteria, discounted cash flow, replacement and timing decisions, risk, depreciation, and income tax.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Basic Statistical Methods
courses.description: Point and interval estimation of systems parameters, statistical decision making about differences in system parameters, analysis and modeling of relationships between variables.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2027 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level CS 1301 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CS 1371 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Methods of Quality Improvement
courses.description: Topics include quality system requirements, designed experiments, process capability analysis, measurement capability, statistical process control, and acceptance sampling plans. Credit will not be awarded for both ISYE 3039 and ISYE 6382.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Simulation Analysis and Design
courses.description: Discrete event simulation methodology emphasizing the statistical basis for simulation modeling and analysis. Overview of computer languages and simulation design applied to various industrial situations.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Supply Chain Modeling: Logistics
courses.description: Course focuses on engineering design concepts and optimization models for logistics decision making in three modules: supply chain design, planning and execution, and transportation.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Supply Chain Modeling: Manufacturing and Warehousing
courses.description: Design and operation of manufacturing and warehousing facilities.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Cornerstone Design for Industrial Engineers
courses.description: Structure a complex problem through information gathering, data analysis, industrial engineering and design principles application, project management, while working in and leading diverse teams.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Engineering Optimization
courses.description: Topics include modeling with networks and graphs; linear, nonlinear, and integer programming, construction of models employing modern modeling languages; and general solution strategies.
courses.prereqText: ISYE 2027 or MATH 3215 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3235 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3236 (minimum grade C); MATH 2603 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3215 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3235 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3236 (minimum grade C); CS 2316 or MATH 3215 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3235 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3236 (minimum grade C).
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2027 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2602 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2603 Minimum Grade of C) and Undergraduate Semester level CS 2316 Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3215 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3225 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3235 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3236 Minimum Grade of C)

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Stochastic Manufacturing and Service Systems
courses.description: Methods for describing stochastic movements of material in manufacturing facilities, supply chain, and equipment maintenance networks. Includes analysis of congestion, delays, and inventory ordering policies.
courses.prereqText: ISYE 2027 or MATH 3215 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3235 (minimum grade C) or MATH 3236 (minimum grade C).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2027 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3215 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3225 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3235 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3236 Minimum Grade of C

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Statistics and Applications
courses.description: Introduction to probability, probability distributions, point estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, linear regression, and analysis of variance. Crosslisted with MATH 3770 and CEE 3770. Also, credit not awarded for both ISYE 3770 and MATH 3670.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2550 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2551 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2561 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X51 Minimum Grade of T and (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1522 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1553 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1554 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1564 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1X53 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1X54 Minimum Grade of T))

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
courses.description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on cognitive science. Interdisciplinary approaches to issues in cognition, including memory, language, problem solving, learning, perception, and action. Crosslisted with CS, PST, and PSYC 3790.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Courses in special topics of timely interest to the profession conducted by resident or visiting faculty.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Design of Human-Integrated Systems
courses.description: Topics include cognitive systems engineering, human information processing, learning, interface and interaction design, task analysis, multimodal human data analysis, usability and performance evaluation in intelligent systems.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2028 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level CS 1322 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Regression and Forecasting
courses.description: Regression analysis: multiple linear regression, diagnostics, and variable selection. Forecasting: exponential smoothing techniques and autoregressive moving average models.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Decision and Data Analytics
courses.description: This course integrates decision and data analytics to solve real-world business problems. It includes hands-on system modeling, data collection and analysis, and reporting writing projects.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level CS 4400 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 4031 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Simulation
courses.description: Advanced modeling and statistical concepts in discrete-event simulations; Monte Carlo simulation; estimation of error and risk; advanced input modeling techniques; comparison and optimization of systems.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3044 Minimum Grade of D

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Senior Design
courses.description: Senior design project requiring student to formulate a project plan with an off-campus enterprise. Includes specific milestones, targets, and evaluation criteria.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3025 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3044 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 4031 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Supply Chain Logistics
courses.description: This course is a follow-up to ISyE 3103 that covers optimization models and case studies for logistics network design and logistics operations.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3103 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Workflow Modeling, Analysis & Design in Manufacturing & Service
courses.description: Introduction to the modeling, analysis and design of workflow systems in manufacturing systems and service systems such as healthcare systems, banks, service centers and warehouses.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Modeling and Analysis of Workflow Systems
courses.description: In-depth modeling and analysis of the workflow dynamics shaping the operation and performance of production and service systems. Application of stochastic modeling in practical problems.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Optimization
courses.description: Theory and implementation of practical methods to find good or optimal solutions to optimization problems too large or complex to solve in a straightforward way.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Constraint Programming
courses.description: This course is an introduction to constraint programming, from its modeling language to its computational methodology and its applications to scheduling, routing, and resource allocation.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CS 2316 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Optimization Foundations for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: An overview of the foundations and algorithms for solving nonlinear continuous optimization problems with special emphasis on the applications to machine learning and artificial intelligence.
courses.prereqText: MATH 1553 or MATH 1554; MATH 2550 or MATH 2551; CS 1301 or CS 1371.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1553 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1554 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2550 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2551 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level CS 1301 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CS 1371 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Stochastic Systems
courses.description: The course will cover Jackson Networks and Markov Decision Processes with applications to production/inventory systems, customer contact centers, revenue management, and health care.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Economics
courses.description: The course studies techniques for coordination and collaboration in supply chains. Applications include pricing strategies, revenue management, gaming, and incentives.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Capital Investment Analysis
courses.description: Students learn core concepts and techniques for economic decision and analysis of complex capital investment problems that involve dimensions of time, uncertainty and strategy.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3025 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3232 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Energy, Efficiency, and Sustainability
courses.description: Analysis and modeling of energy production and use, material and energy efficiency, sustainability, and cost for systems, products, and services.
courses.prereqText: ISYE 3025 (minimum grade C) or MGT 3076 (minimum grade C); PHYS 2211; MGT 2255 or MATH 2550 (minimum grade C).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3025 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level MGT 3076 Minimum Grade of C and Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level MGT 2255 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2251 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2550 Minimum Grade of C

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Public Health Systems
courses.description: This course provides an overview of health systems and public health to explore their positive impact on well-being of individuals and effectiveness of health systems.
courses.prereqText: ISYE 3770 or BMED 2400 or ISYE 3030 or ISYE 2028.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3770 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 2400 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Intelligent Healthcare Delivery Systems
courses.description: Healthcare systems involve patients, providers, insurers and regulators aiming to optimize quality, access, efficiency. Topics include systems engineering methods to analyze and design healthcare systems.
courses.prereqText: ISYE 3030 or ISYE 2028 or ISYE 3770 or CEE 3770 or ECE 3077 or ECON 2250 or PUBP 3120 or BMED 2400; MATH 2551 or MATH 2550.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3770 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CEE 3770 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3077 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECON 2250 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3120 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 2400 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2551 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2550 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Methods and Applications of Machine Learning
courses.description: This course introduces the available methods in machine learning, which methods are better in what situations, objective functions and errors, and how to tune parameters.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Online Learning & Decision Making
courses.description: Fundamental theoretical tools for analyzing online methods, algorithmic techniques for developing computationally efficient methods, applications to real-world problems, and discussion around ethical and legal issues.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3133 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Bio-Inspired Design
courses.description: We examine evolutionary adaptation as a course for engineering design inspiration, utilizing principles of scaling, adaptability, and robust multifunctionality that characterize biological systems. Credit not allowed for both ISYE 4740 and (BIOL 4740, or PTFE 4740 or MSE 4740 or ME 4740 ).

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special Topics.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Organizational Behavior for Engineers
courses.description: Studies the scientific generation, formalization, and application of the knowledge of individual and group behaviors that engineers need to function effectively within contexts.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Constraint Programming
courses.description: This course is an introduction to constraint programming, from its modeling language to its computational methodology and its applications to scheduling, routing, and resource allocation.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Manufacturing Systems
courses.description: Topics include analysis of flows, bottlenecks and queuing, types of operations, manufacturing inventories, aggregreate production planning, lot sizes and lead times, and pull production systems.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Warehousing Systems
courses.description: Topics include design and analysis of materials handling systems, warehouse layout, order picking strategies, warehousing inventories, warehouse management systems, integration of production and distribution systems. Credit will not be awarded for both ISYE 6202 and ISYE 6383.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Transportation and Supply Chain Systems
courses.description: Topics include supply chain characterization, site location, mode selection, distribution planning, vehicle routing, demand management, replenishment management, geographic information systems, and real-time control issues. Credit will not be awarded for both ISYE 6203 and ISYE 6383.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Cognitive Engineering
courses.description: Application of cognitive science concepts to system design, and the development of concepts appropriate for understanding and aiding cognition in naturally or technologically complex environments.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Models in Human-Machine Systems
courses.description: The development and use of mathematical models of human behavior are considered. Approaches from estimation theory, control theory, queuing theory, and fuzzy set theory are considered.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Understanding and Supporting Human Decision Making
courses.description: Prescriptive and descriptive theories of human decision making are discussed/contrasted. Approaches to aiding human decision making are considered in context of these theoretical frameworks.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Topics in Human-Integrated Systems
courses.description: State-of-the-art research directions including supervisory control models of human command control tasks; human-computer interface in scheduling and supervision of flexible manufacturing systems.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Engineering Economy
courses.description: Advanced engineering economy topics, including economic worth, economic optimization under constraints, risk and uncertainty, foundations of utility theory.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Financial Engineering
courses.description: Advanced techniques for economic analysis of capital investment. Basic terminology and financial engineering concepts for managing and valuing project risk. Real options applications in systems engineering.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Productivity Measurement and Analysis
courses.description: Modern measurement of productivity measurement and analysis including principles, issues, and latest techniques associated with benchmarking, efficiency measurement, and productivity tracking. Empirical studies and group projects.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Economic Decision Analysis
courses.description: Topics include preferences and utilities, social choice, equilibrium concepts, noncooperative and cooperative game theory, price mechanisms, auction mechanisms, voting theory, and incentive compatibility.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Design of Human-integrated Systems
courses.description: Analysis and design of complex work domains in technological environments. Credit not allowed for both ISYE 6231 and AE 6721.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Scheduling Theory
courses.description: Includes topics in sequencing and scheduling with emphasis on deterministic machine scheduling problems with some stochastic results examined. Complexity of various problems will be analyzed.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Public Impact Applications of Operations Research and Management Science
courses.description: The focus is on the health and public applications of Operations Research. Students will complete a group project with a non-profit organization and discuss papers.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Statistics for Supply Chain Engineering
courses.description: Collection, management, and analysis of supply chain data.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Finance for Supply Chain Engineering
courses.description: Investment and analysis of operating capital.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Operations Research for Supply Chain Engineering I
courses.description: Deterministic models of supply chains including location and material flow. Optimization techniques including linear programming, network flows, integer programming, and heuristics.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Operations Research fo Supply Chain Engineering II
courses.description: Probabilistic models of supply chains, including the effects of variability; models of wholesale and retail demand; forecasting and simulation.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Engineering I
courses.description: Production scheduling; inventory systems; warehousing, including stocking strategies, order-picking, sortation, automation; distribution.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Engineering II
courses.description: Transportation: truck-load and less-than-truckload, and package-courier systems; container shipping, including port operations, steamship scheduling; railroad operations, including intermodal; air cargo. The international freight network and patterns of freight flow. Management and recirculation of trailers/containers. Labor issues.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Engineering III
courses.description: Problems of coordination and collaboration along the supply chain; make-or-buy decisions; pricing and auctions; wholesale and retail channels; supply chain dynamics, including the bullwhip effect. Distinctive supply chain issues in key economies.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Suppply Chain Strategy
courses.description: Case studies of notable supply chains successes and failures.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Information Systems
courses.description: Planning and executing systems for inventory, warehousing, transportation, import/export, etc. Services-oriented architecture, cloud computing; systems integration; RFID and other technologies for scanning and monitoring.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Supply Chain Engineering Seminar
courses.description: Through a program of industry speakers and facility tours, student will learn to assess and critique supply chain practice.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Capstone Project for Supply Chain Engineering I
courses.description: Small groups of students undertake an industry-sponsored project under faculty guidance.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Capstone Project for Supply Chain Engineering II
courses.description: Small groups of students undertake an industry-sponsored project under faculty guidance.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Production Planning and Control
courses.description: Fundamentals of Production Planning and Lean Manufacturing.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Manufacturing Reliability
courses.description: Fundamentals of Reliability and Maintainability Engineering.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Quality Control and Six Sigma
courses.description: Fundamentals of Quality Control and Six Sigma Methods. Credit will not be awarded for both ISYE 6382 and ISYE 3039.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Manufacturing Supply Chain Operations
courses.description: Fundamentals of Manufacturing Supply Chain Operations. Credit will not be awarded for both ISYE 6383 and ISYE 6202 or ISYE 6383 and ISYE 6203.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Time Series Analysis
courses.description: Basic forecasting methods, ARIMA models, transfer functions.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Nonparametric Data Analysis
courses.description: Nonparametric statistics and basic categorical data analysis.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Statistical Methods for Manufacturing Design and Improvement
courses.description: Fractional factorial designs, response surface methods.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Theoretical Statistics
courses.description: Rigorous introduction to theory of statistical inference. Estimation and testing. Construction and assessment of estimators and tests. Fundamentals of decision theory, minimax, and Bayes Paradigms.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
courses.description: Analysis of variance, full and fractional factoral designs at two and three levels, orthogonal arrays, response surface methodology, robust parameter design for production/process improvement.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Statistical Modeling and Regression Analysis
courses.description: Simple and multiple linear regression, inferences and diagnostics, stepwise regression and model selection, advanced regression methods, basic design and analysis of experiments, factorial analysis.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Computational Statistics
courses.description: This class describes the available knowledge regarding statistical computing. Topics include random deviates generation, importance sampling, Monte Carlo Markov chain (MCMC), EM algorithms, bootstrapping, model selection criteria, (e.g. C-p, AIC, etc.) splines, wavelets, and Fourier transform.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Theory and Practice of Bayesian Statistics
courses.description: Rigorous introduction to the theory of Beysian Statistical Inference. Bayesian estimation and testing. Conjugate priors. Noninformative priors. Bayesian computation. Bayesian networks and Bayesian signal processing. Various engineering applications.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Biostatistics
courses.description: An introduction to fundamental ideas and techniques in Biostatistics, with an emphasis on conceptual understanding and on the analysis of real data sets.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Introduction to Analytics Modeling
courses.description: An introduction to important and commonly-used models in analytics, as well as aspects of the modeling process.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: High Dimensional Data Analytics
courses.description: A variety of topics such as functional data analysis, image processing, multilinear algebra and tensor analysis, and regularization in high-dimensional regression.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Resilient Networks
courses.description: Optimization and game-theoretic methods for designing, analyzing, and operating resilient networked systems under uncertainty and disruptions, with applications to transportation, energy distribution, and supply chains.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Simulation
courses.description: Covers modeling of discrete-event dynamic systems and introduces methods for using these models to solve engineering design and analysis problems.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Monte Carlo Methods
courses.description: Covers state-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulation techniques. These techniques will be used to model and solve a variety of real-world problems from several diverse areas in science and engineering, including supply chain analysis and design, pattern recognition, VLSI design, network reliability, financial engineering, and molecular biology.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Probabilistic Models and Their Applications
courses.description: An introduction to basic stochastic processes such as Poisson and Markov processes and their applications in areas such as inventory, reliability, and queueing.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Queuing Theory
courses.description: Processing networks with queuing. Performance analysis using Markov process description of system behavior. Applications and numerical studies in manufacturing, system maintainability, computer systems, telecommunication networks.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Linear Optimization
courses.description: Theory, algorithms, and applications of linear programming. Topics include the simplex method and resolution of degeneracy, duality and sensitivity analysis, basis factorization, the dual and revised simplex methods, and geometry of polyhedra. Intended for Ph.D. students.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Discrete Optimization
courses.description: Fundamentals of integer and combinatorial optimization. Topics include polyhedra, cuts, Lagrangean duality, complexity, and others. This course is intended for Ph.D. students.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Nonlinear Optimization
courses.description: Fundamentals of nonlinear optimization. Topics include optimality conditions; convex programming and duality; unconstrained and constrained methods. Polynomial algorithms and interior point methods. Dual methods. This course is for students seriously considering a PhD.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Stochastic Optimization
courses.description: An introduction to sequential decision making under uncertainty. Much of the course is devoted to the theoretical, modeling, and computational aspects of Markov decision processes.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Deterministic Optimization
courses.description: An introduction to deterministic optimization methodologies including approaches from linear, discrete, and nonlinear optimization including algorithms and computations. Applications will be introduced as appropriate.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Financial Optimization Models
courses.description: An introduction to optimization techniques with special emphasis on applications to finance, including portfolio optimization, immunization, and risk management.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Computational Methods in Optimization
courses.description: Strategies and techniques for converting optimization theory into effective computational procedures. Emphasis is on applications in linear, integer, and nonlinear programming; networks and graphs.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Energy Technology and Policy
courses.description: Examines energy production, use, and production, use, and policy using quantitative engineering and policy analysis. Addresses resource constraints, physical principles, and policy analysis methods.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Life Cycle Assessment
courses.description: Methods and applications for life cycle assessment of environmental impacts of products, services, and decisions, with process-based and input-output modeling for attributional and consequential analyses.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Basic Statistical Methods
courses.description: Overview of basic tools used in statistical analysis and modeling. Credit not allowed to students seeking a degree in ISYE.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Computational Data Analysis: Learning, Mining, and Computation
courses.description: Theoretical/computational foundations of analyzing large/complex modern datasets, including the fundamental concepts of machine learning and data mining needed for both resesarch and practice. Crosslisted with CSE 6740. Credit not awarded for both ISYE 6740 and CS 4641 /7641/ CSE 6740.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Applied Analytics Practicum
courses.description: Practical analytics project experience applying ideas from the classroom to a significant project of interest to a business, government agency, or other organization.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Stochastic Processes in Finance
courses.description: Mathematical modeling of financial markets, derivative securities pricing, and portfolio optimization. Concepts from probability and mathematics are introduced as needed. Crosslisted with MATH 6759.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Stochastic Processes I
courses.description: Discrete time Markov chains, Poisson and renewal processes; transient and limiting behavior; average cost and utility measures of systems. Intended for Ph.D students. Crosslisted with MATH 6761.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Stochastic Processes II
courses.description: Continuous time Markov chains; uniformization, transient and limiting behavior; Brownian motion and martingales; optional sampling and convergence. Intended for Ph.D. students. Crosslisted with MATH 6762.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Design and Implementation of Systems to Support
courses.description: Introduction to large-scale system design to support computational finance for options, stocks, or other financial instruments. Some programming experience and previous exposure to stocks, bonds, and options required. Crosslisted with MATH 6767.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Fixed Income Securities
courses.description: Description, institutional features, and mathematical modeling of fixed income securities. Use of both deterministic and stochastic models. Crosslisted with MATH 6769.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Managing Resources of the Technological Firm
courses.description: This course explores the competitive advantage manufacturing and service firms derive from the effective management of their technology, workforce, materials, and information resources. Crosslisted with MGT 6772.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Reliability Theory
courses.description: Structural properties and reliability of coherent systems.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Statistical Techniques of Financial Data Analysis
courses.description: Fundamentals of statistical inference for models used in the modern analysis of financial data. Crosslisted with MATH 6783.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: The Practice of Quantitative and Computational Finance
courses.description: Case studies, visiting lecturers from financial institutions, student group projects of an advanced nature, and student reports, all centered around quantitative and computational finance. Crosslisted with MATH and MGT 6785.

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Systems Monitoring and Prognostics
courses.description: The course focuses on sensor-based condition monitoring techniques, modeling of degradation processes, fault diagnostics and prognostics of failures in engineering systems using stochastic and statistical methods.

courses.description: Theory, algorithms, and applications of computer simulation. Topics include generalized semi-Markov processes; input-output analysis; random number, variate, and sample path generation; variance reduction techniques; and optimization via simulation. This course is intended for Ph.D. students.

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Nonlinear Programming

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Combinatorial Optimization
courses.description: Typical coverage includes: Matching theory, network optimization, traversals in graphs, integrality of polyhedra, matroids, covers, cliques, and stable sets.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Advanced Integer Programming
courses.description: General integer modeling concepts; valid inequalities and facets; duality; general algorithms such as branch-and-bound and branch-and-cut; special purpose algorithms; applications.

courses.subject: ISYE
courses.title: Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning

courses.subject: ISYE

courses.description: Explores various concepts of the state in international affairs as well as the concepts of sovereignty and revolution.

courses.subject: INTA
