courses.description: The course provides comprehensive knowledge of the manufacture of nontraditional products from forest biomaterials. It analyzes and assesses emerging manufacturing technologies, materials and products.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2140 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Biologically Inspired Design
courses.description: We examine evolutionary adaptation as a source for engineering design inspiration, utilizing principles of scaling, adaptability, and robust multifunctionality that characterize biological systems. Credit not allowed for both MSE 4740 and (BIOL 4740 or ISYE 4740 or ME 4740 ).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1520 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3100 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Introduction to Biomaterials
courses.description: Introduction to different classes of biomaterials (polymers, metals, ceramics) and physiological responses to biomaterial implantation. Topics include material properties, host response, and biomaterial characterization techniques. Crosslisted with BMED 4751.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Electronics Packaging Assembly, Reliability, Thermal Management, and Test
courses.description: The course provides hands-on instruction in electronics packaging, including assembly, reliability, thermal management, and test of next-generation microsystems. Crosslisted with ECE and ME 4754.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3040 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3710 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Electronic Packaging Substrate Fabrication
courses.description: This course provides students with hands-on instruction in basic SOP concepts and techniques, including interconnect design, substrate material selection and properties, photodielectric deposition, via formation and photolithography, copper metallization, and finally, substrate testing. Laboratory instructions are augmented by an interactive multimedia educational presentation that makes the course work material remotely accessible via the internet.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2551 or MATH 2561; MATH 2552 or MATH 2562; CHEM 1211K; PHYS 2212.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2401 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2411 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 24X1 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2551 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X51 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2561 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2403 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2413 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 24X3 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2552 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X52 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2562 Minimum Grade of D) and Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1211K Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2212 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Electrochemical Energy Storage and Conversion
courses.description: An elective class for senior-level students interested in electrochemical storage and conversion, including the fundamentals of electrochemistry and practical battery and fueld cells. Cross-listed with ChBE and ME 4759.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Industrial Controls and Manufacturing
courses.description: Students are introduced to industrial controls and the fundamentals of manufacturing with hands-on experience based on lab projects using industry software and hardware for communications and control. Credit not allowed for MSE 4761.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3710 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fabrication and Properties of Nanoscale Devices
courses.description: Fundamental properties at the nanoscale for photonics and sensors. Nanoscale fabrication methods including thin films, ion beam, lithography, electroplating, and example case studies in NEMS/MEMS and photonics. Credit not allowed for both MSE 4766 and ME 4766.
courses.prereqText: ME 3322 or ME 3720 or PHYS 3141 or MSE 3001.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3720 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level AE 3450 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 3141 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering I: Formation and Properties
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry, structure, and formation of polymers, physical states and transitions, physical and mechanical properties of polymer fluids and solids. Crosslisted with CHE, CHEM, and ME 4775.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 2312 or CHEM 1315; CHEM 3411 or MSE 3001 or CHBE 2130 or CHBE 2140 or ME 3322.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 2312 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1315 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 3411 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2130 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2140 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering II: Analysis, Processing, and Laboratory
courses.description: Polymer fabrication processes and methods of characterization and identification of polymers are presented. Experiments in polymerization, processing, and property evaluation of polymers. Crosslisted with CHE, CHEM, ME, and TFE 4776.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PTFE 4775 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials Selection and Design
courses.description: Principles of selecting materials and processes for engineering applications. Methodologies for designing new materials and conceiving hybrid solutions. Credit not allowed for both MSE 4790 and ME 4213 (or ME 4790 ).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level COE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Composites
courses.description: Introduction to properties and structures of common matrix and reinforcing materials, mechanics of fiber-reinforced composites, lamina and laminate analysis, and mechanical performance. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 4791.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3005 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Composite Materials and Processing
courses.description: Basic principles of selecting component materials and manufacturing composites are presented. Polymeric, metallic, and ceramic systems are considered. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 4793.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1310 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1211K Minimum Grade of D) and Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2212 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Composite Materials and Manufacturing
courses.description: Basic principles of selection and design of composite materials and their manufacturing and testing. Cost factors. Laboratory exercises on manufacturing and tests. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 4794.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamental Elements of Nuclear Reactor Materials
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of nuclear reactor materials. Topics covered are basics of radiation damage, defect creation and evolution, microstructure-property correlations in cladding and fuel of nuclear materials.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: special topics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Functional Materials
courses.description: This course focuses on the effects of defects on physical properties; charge/mass transport; semiconductors, heterojunctions, electrical and magnetic polarization, interaction processes between various physical properties; electrical characterization techniques.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Transmission Electron Microscopy
courses.description: Introduction to the kinematical electron scattering theory, optics in TEM, diffraction contrast imaging of defects, dynamical electron diffraction effects; and chemical microanalysis using EDS.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Quantitative Characterization of Microstructures
courses.description: Application of statistically unbiased methods for estimating geometrical attributes of microstructures and nonplanar fracture surfaces from plane sections and projections, digital image analysis, and computer simulations of microstructures.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Surface Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to vacuum science and technology; structure of solid surfaces; electron and ion energy analyzers, electron spectroscopies (e.g., AES and XPS); ion-based techniques (e.g., SIMS and RBS); depth profiling; ion channeling.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Computational Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: This course aims to provide a broad understanding of a spectrum of modern state-of-the-art computational methods used in materials science and engineering.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Defects
courses.description: Emphasis on the origin and character of point, line, and surface defects in crystalline materials and their influence on mechanical, chemical, magnetic, optical, and electronic properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials for Energy Storage and Conversion
courses.description: Scientific principles concerning the transfer, capture, and storage of energy harnessed from various sources, including solar, wind, geothermal, and biomass.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Soft Nanomaterials and Nanostructures
courses.description: Fundamentals and applications of soft (polymer and biological) nanomaterials such as colloidal assemblies, self-assembled structures, energy devices, photonic materials, drug delivery, flexible electronics, soft robotics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: To examine the principles of thermodynamics as applied to equilibria associated with solutions, mixtures, chemical reactions, and interfaces in materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Crystallography, Structure and Defects
courses.description: Provides students with a fundamental understanding of crystal structures, symmetry, origin, character, defects in crystalline materials, and the influence of these defects on different properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Kinetics of Phase Transformations
courses.description: To introduce the fundamentals of thermodynamics and mathematics to the kinetics of diffusional and non-diffusional phase transformation in engineering materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Scattering Theory
courses.description: A general introduction to the scattering/diffraction of electromagnetic radiation from solids. The kinematical formalism is developed emphasizing x-ray scattering as a characterization tool.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Nanomaterials
courses.description: Topics include the synthesis and growth processes controlling quantum dot formation, nanowires, and three- dimensional self-assembled nanostructures. Additional characterization techniques and emerging applications are presented.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Corrosion of Materials
courses.description: To introduce students to the basic kinetic mechanisms associated with the interactions of materials with liquids and gases.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics - MSE
courses.description: Fundamental of quantum mechanics of atoms, molecules and solids necessary for engineers to understand the electronic, optical and thermal properties of inorganic and organic materials.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Corrosion
courses.description: Course covers thermodynamics, and kinetics of metallic corrosion in electrolytes and high-temperature oxidation. Different forms of corrosion, their mechanisms, and corrosion control methods are discussed.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: This course introduces structural features of materials, including point/space groups, representative crystal structures, quasi-crystals, amorphous and rubbery state, liquid crystals, colloids, solutions, and effect of symmetry on properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Structure of Materials
courses.description: This course introduces structural features of materials, including point/space groups, representative crystal structures, quasi-crystals, amorphous and rubbery state, liquid crystals, colloids, solutions, and effect of symmetry on properties.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymers for Electronic and Photonic Applications I
courses.description: Review of fundamentals and principles of polymers used in electronics and photonics; relationships between the advances of semiconductor technology and the importance of polymers and their applications.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Polymer Processing
courses.description: Common polymer processing techniques and recent advancement; Modeling of polymer processing focusing on how to build a sound model; Computer aided engineering for polymer processing.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Natural Polymers
courses.description: The structures and properties of natural products are presented. Production of cellulose and proteins in discussed. Credit not allowed for both MSE 6603 and PTFE 6301.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Materials Science of Cellular Components
courses.description: Addresses structure-property relationship of cellular components. Credit not allowed for both MSE 6730 and BMED 6730.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Preparation & Reactions of Polymers
courses.description: A detailed treatment of the reactions involved in the synthesis of both human-made and natural polymers, including preparation and degradative reactions of polymer systems.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymer Solutions
courses.description: Study of polymer solutions, polymer miscibility, adsorption, sorptions, plasticization, molecular weights, molecular weight distribution, and interfacial phenomena using thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. Crosslisted with CHEM, CHE, and PTFE 6751.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Characterization
courses.description: This course introduces the student to surface, near-surface and structural methods of polymer characterization. Specialized techniques critical to physical structure are emphasized. Crosslisted with CHEM, CHE, and PTFE 6752.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Engineering Communication
courses.description: Writing and editing engineering documents; designing and explaining visuals; creating and delivering electronic presentations. Crosslisted with CEE 6754.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Theoretical Chemistry of Polymers
courses.description: Thermodynamics and microscopic dynamics of polymers. Fundamental concepts, including scaling concepts, governing anisotropy of polarizability, phase transitions, morphology, time-dependent correlations, etc. are discussed. Crosslisted with CHEM and PTFE 6755.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced topics in synthetic polymerization methodology, polymer structure, and polymer properties in solution and the solid state.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Structure, Physical Properties, and Characterization
courses.description: Formulations and analysis of molecular and phenomenological models of elastic and viscoelastic behavior, development and description of structure, and fundamental aspects of structure-property relations. Crosslisted with TFE, CHE, and ME 6768.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymer Communications
courses.description: Oral and written presentation of modern polymer topics, with an emphasis on constructive and ethical critical thinking in a group setting.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Integrated Low-cost Microelectronics Systems Packaging
courses.description: Broad overview of system-level, cross-disciplinary microelectronics packaging technologies, including design, test, thermal, reliability, optoelectronics, and RF integration. Comparison of system-to-chip and system-to-package. Crosslisted with ECE and ME 6776.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Biomaterials
courses.description: Advanced topics of biomaterials performance and engineering, including biointerfaces, host reactions to materials, and bio-inspired/smart-materials strategies. Crosslisted with BMED, CHE, and ME 6777.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Mathematical, Statistical, and Computational Techniques in Materials Science
courses.description: Fundamental physical, analytical, and mathematical techniques encountered in materials engineering including stress and strain, crystallographic and orientation transformations, X-ray, TEM, and solid-state concepts are emphasized. Crosslisted with ME and PTFE 6795.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Structure-Property Relationships in Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the multi-scale structure effects on material properties. Course will prepare students for future in-depth courses. Crosslisted with PTFE and ME 6796.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Electroceramics
courses.description: Defects chemistry; electrochemical and electrophysical behavior of metallic/semiconducting ceramics, dielectrics, and ferrites; device applications of various electronic ceramics.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Impedance and Dielectric Spectroscopy
courses.description: The basic theory of how current, voltage, and phase angle measurements over a wide frequency range (typically mHz-MHz) can provide information about microstructural features at all length scales.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Dislocation and Deformation Mechanics
courses.description: Emphasis on interactions of dislocations with other defects, dislocation dynamics, and their correlation with mechanical properties under different rates of loading.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Solidification Processing
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics, kinetics, mass transport, and physical materials are applied to the development of microstructure during solidification.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Polymers for Electronic and Photonic Applications II
courses.description: Review of fundamentals and principles of polymers used in electronics and photonics. The relationship between the recent advances of semiconductor technology and the importance of polymers will be discussed.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Students will learn about what it takes to be a faculty through sills needed for “delivery of lecture” via the practice of teaching.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Mechanics of Polymer Solids and Fluids
courses.description: Continuum mechanics of solids and fluids; mechanics of deformation of anisotropic polymers; yield, breaking and fatigue; non-Newtonian vioscous and viscoelastic behavior of polymer fluids. Crosslisted with CHE, ME and PTFE 7771.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Fracture Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced study of failure of structural materials under load, mechanics of fracture, and microscopic and macroscopic aspects of the fracture of engineering materials. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 7772.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Fatigue of Materials and Structures
courses.description: Mechanical and microstructural aspects of nucleation and growth of cracks under cyclic loading conditions, notch effects, cumulative damage, multiaxial loading, and fatigue crack propagation. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and ME 7774.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Mechanics of Composites
courses.description: Anisotropic elasticity, hygrothermal behavior, stress analysis of laminated composites including 3-D effects, stress concentrations, free-edge effects, thick laminates, adhesive and mechanical connections, fracture of composites. Crosslisted with AE, CHE, CEE, ME, and PTFE 7792.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Manufacturing of Composites
courses.description: Major manufacturing techniques for metal, ceramic, and polymer composites. Modeling of processes with emphasis on fundamental mechanisms and effects. Crosslisted with AE, CHE, CEE, ME, and PTFE 7793.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: The latest advances in research and development will be presented by the enrolled students from articles in recent issues of recognized periodicals.

courses.subject: MSE
courses.title: Advanced Presentation Skills
courses.description: Designing and explaining visuals; creating and delivering scientific electronic presentations; learning to speak and present to a variety of audiences.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topic offerings of current interest not included in regular courses.

courses.description: For graduate students holding teaching assistantships.

courses.title: Research Assistantship
courses.description: For graduate students holding a research assistantship.

courses.title: GT-PKU

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Support for Precalculus
courses.description: Practicum for Learning Support students enrolled in MATH 1113 (Precalculus).

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Support for College Algebra
courses.description: This Learning Support course provides corequisite support in mathematics for students enrolled in MATH 1111 – College Algebra. Topics will parallel topics being studied in MATH 1111 and the course will provide support for the essential quantitative skills needed to be successful in MATH 1111. Taken with MATH 1111, this course provides an in-depth study of the properties of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions as needed for calculus. Emphasis is on using algebraic and graphical techniques for solving problems involving linear, quadratic, piece-wise defined, rational, polynomial, exponential and logarithmic functions.

Emphasis is on using algebraic and graphical techniques for solving problems involving linear, quadratic, piece-wise defined, rational, polynomial, exponential and logarithmic functions.

courses.title: Pre-calculus

May only be used for degree credit with departmental approval.

courses.title: Integral Calculus

courses.description: An introduction to linear alegbra including eigenvalues and eigenvectors, applications to linear systems, least squares. Credit not awarded for both MATH 1553 and MATH 1522, MATH 1502, MATH 1504, MATH 1512, MATH 1554 or MATH 1564.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Linear algebra eigenvalues, eigenvectors, applications to linear systems, least squares, diagnolization, quadratic forms.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra with Abstract Vector Spaces
courses.description: This is an intensive first course in linear algebra including the theories of linear transformations and abstract vector spaces. Credit not awarded for both MATH 1564 and MATH 1553, MATH 1554, MATH 1522, MATH 1502, MATH 1504 or MATH 1512.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Finite Mathematics
courses.description: Linear equations, matrices, linear programming, sets and counting, probability and statistics.

courses.title: Survey of Calculus
courses.description: Techniques of differentiation, integration, application of integration to probability and statistics, multidimensional calculus. Credit not allowed for both MATH 1712 and 1501.

courses.title: Foundations of Mathematical Proof
courses.description: An introduction to proofs in advanced mathematics, intended as a transition to upper division courses including Abstract Algebra I and Analysis I.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Vectors in three dimensions, curves in space, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, optimization, integration of functions of several variables. Vector Calculus not covered. Credit will not be awarded for both MATH 2550 and MATH 2605 or MATH 2401 or MATH 2551 or MATH 1555.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Multivariable Calculus
courses.description: Multivariable calculus: Linear approximation and Taylor's theorems, Lagrange multiples and constrained optimization, multiple integration and vector analysis including the theorems of Green, Gauss, and Stokes. Credit will not be awarded for both MATH 2551 and MATH 2401 or MATH 2411 or MATH 2561.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.description: Methods for obtaining numerical and analytic solutions of elementary differential equations. Applications are also discussed with an emphasis on modeling. Credit not awarded for both MATH 2552 and MATH 2403 or MATH 2413 or MATH 2562.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Multivariable Calculus

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Graduate Studies in Mathematics
courses.description: This course covers practical information helping students start their careers as a professional mathematician. It also satisfies the Georgia Tech RCR requirements for "in-person" training.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Graph Theory and Combinatorial Structures
courses.description: Fundamentals, connectivity, matchings, colorings, extremal problems, Ramsey theory, planar graphs, perfect graphs. Applications to operations research and the design of efficient algorithms.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Linear Algebra
courses.description: An advanced course in Linear Algebra and applications.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modern Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: Graduate-level linear and abstract algebra including groups, finite fields, classical matrix groups and bilinear forms, multilinear algebra, and matroids. First of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modern Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: Graduate-level linear and abstract algebra including rings, fields, modules, some algebraic number theory and Galois theory. Second of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability Theory for Scientists and Engineers
courses.description: Classical introduction to probability theory including expectation, notions of convergence, laws of large numbers, independence, large deviations, conditional expectation, martingales, and Markov chains.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability I
courses.description: Develops the probability basis requisite in modern statistical theories and stochastic processes. Topics of this course include measure and integration foundations of probability, distribution functions, convergence concepts, laws of large numbers, and central limit theory. First of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability II
courses.description: Develops the probability basis requisite in modern statistical theories and stochastic processes. Topics of this course include results for sums of independent random variables, Markov processes, martingales, Poisson processes, Brownian motion, conditional probability and conditional expectation, and topics from ergodic theory. Second of two classes.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Statistical Inference I
courses.description: Basic theories of statistical estimation, including optimal estimation in finite samples and asymptotically optimal estimation. A careful mathematical treatment of the primary techniques of estimation utilized by statisticians.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Testing Statistical Hypotheses
courses.description: Basic theories of testing statistical hypotheses, including a thorough treatment of testing in exponential class families. A careful mathematical treatment of the primary techniques of hypothesis testing utilized by statisticians.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Statistical Models
courses.description: Basic unifying theory underlying techniques of regression, analysis of variance and covariance, from a geometric point of view. Modern computational capabilities are exploited fully. Students apply the theory to real data through canned and coded programs.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Multivariate Statistical Analysis
courses.description: Multivariate normal distribution theory, correlation and dependence analysis, regression and prediction, dimension-reduction methods, sampling distributions and related inference problems, selected applications in classification theory, multivariate process control, and pattern recognition.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations I
courses.description: This sequence develops the qualitative theory for systems of ordinary differential equations. Topics include stability, Lyapunov functions, Floquet theory, attractors, invariant manifolds, bifurcation theory, normal forms. First of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations II
courses.description: This sequence develops the qualitative theory for systems of differential equations. Topics include stability, Lyapunov functions, Floquet theory, attractors, invariant manifolds, bifurcation theory, and normal forms. Second of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Functions of a Complex Variable I
courses.description: Complex integration, including Goursat's theorem; classification of singularities, the argument principle, the maximum principle; Riemann Mapping theorem; analytic continuation and Riemann surfaces; range of an analytic function, including Picard's theorem.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis I
courses.description: Lebesgue measure and integration, differentiation, abstract measure theory. Credit cannot be received for both MATH 6337 and MATH 6579.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis II
courses.description: Continuation of MATH 6337. L^p and Hilbert spaces, introduction to operator theory and functional analysis. Credit cannot be received for both MATH 6338 and MATH 6580.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations I
courses.description: Introduction to the mathematical theory of partial differential equations covering the basic linear models of science and exact solution techniques.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations II
courses.description: This course covers the general mathematical theory of linear stationary and evolution problems plus selected topics chosen from the instructor's interests.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Geometry I
courses.description: The study of zero sets of polynomials: algebraic varieties, regular and rational mappings, the Zariski topology.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Geometry II
courses.description: A continuation of Algebraic Geometry I.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Topology I
courses.description: Simplicial homology. Chain complexes and acyclic carriers. Simplicial approximation. The exact homology sequence. Maps of spheres. Mayer-Vietoris sequence.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Topology
courses.description: Manifolds. Differentiable structures. Tangent bundles. Embeddings and immersions. Maps on manifolds. Transversality. Morse-Sard Theorem. Vector bundles.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry I
courses.description: Core topics in differential, including: Lie groups, curvature, and relations with topology.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry II
courses.description: Introduces students to topics of current interest in geometry.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Industrial Mathematics I
courses.description: Applied mathematics techniques to solve real-world problems. Topics include mathematical modeling, asymptotic analysis, differential equations and scientific computation. Prepares the student for MATH 6515.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Measure Theory for Scientists and Engineers
courses.description: An introduction to measure theory and Lebesgue integration with a focus on topics that tend to be of the most utility in science and engineering. Credit cannot be received for both MATH 6337 and MATH 6579.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Hilbert Spaces for Scientists and Engineers
courses.description: Structure of linear operators in infinite dimensional spaces, applications. Credit cannot be received for both MATH 6338 and MATH 6580.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Finance
courses.description: Basic numerical and simulation techniques used in the pricing of derivative securities and in related problems in finance. Some programming experience required.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Introduction to the implementation and analysis of numerical algorithms for the numerical solution of the classic partial differential equations of science and engineering. Must have knowledge of a computer programming language, familiarity with partial differential equations and elements of scientific computing.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Analysis and implementation of numerical methods for nonlinear partial differential equations including elliptic, hyperbolic, and/or parabolic problems. Must have knowledge of classic linear partial differential equations and exposure to numerical methods for partial differential equations at the level of MATH 6640 or numerical linear algebra at the level of MATH 6643.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
courses.description: Introduction to the numerical solution of the classic problems of linear algebra including linear systems, least squares, Singular value decomposition, eigenvalue problems. Crosslisted with CSE 6643.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Iterative Methods for Systems of Equations
courses.description: Iterative methods for linear and nonlinear systems of equations including Jacobi, G-S, SOR, CG, multigrid, Newton quasi-Newton, updating, and gradient-based methods. Crosslisted with CSE 6644.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Approximation Theory
courses.description: Theoretical and computational aspects of polynomial, rational, trigonometric, spline, and wavelet approximation.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Methods for Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.description: Analysis and implementation of numerical methods for initial and two-point boundary value problems for ordinary differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Methods for Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Approximation of the dynamical structure of a differential equation and preservation of dynamical structure under discretization. Must be familiar with dynamical systems and numerical methods for initial and boundary value problems in ordinary differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math Methods of Applied Sciences I
courses.description: Review of linear algebra and ordinary differential equations, brief introduction to functions of a complex variable.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math Methods of Applied Sciences II
courses.description: Review of vector calculus and its applications to partial differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes in Finance I
courses.description: Mathematical modeling of financial markets, derivative securities pricing, and portfolio optimization. Concepts from probability and mathematics are introduced as needed. Crosslisted with ISYE 6759.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes I
courses.description: Discrete time Markov chains, Poisson processes, and renewal processes. Transient and limiting behavior. Average cost and utility measures of systems. Algorithms for computing performance measures. Modeling of inventories, and flows in manufacturing and computer networks. Crosslisted with ISYE 6761.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes II
courses.description: Continuous time Markov chains. Uniformization, transient and limiting behavior. Brownian motion and martingales. Optional sampling and convergence. Modeling of inventories, finance, flows in manufacturing and computer networks. Crosslisted with ISYE 6762.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Design and Implementation of Systems to Support
courses.description: Computational Finance Introduction to large scale system design to support computational finance for options, stocks, or other financial instruments. Some programming experience, and previous exposure to stocks, bonds, and options required. Crosslisted with ISYE 6767.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Fixed Income Securities
courses.description: Description, institutional features, and mathematical modeling of fixed income securities. Use of both deterministic and stochastic models. Crosslisted with ISYE 6769.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Statistical Techniques of Financial Data Analysis
courses.description: Fundamentals of statistical inference for models used in the modern analysis of financial data. Crosslisted with ISYE 6783.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: The Practice of Quantitative and Computational Finance
courses.description: Case studies, visiting lecturers from financial institutions, student group projects of an advanced nature, and student reports, all centered around quantitative and computational finance. Crosslisted with ISYE and MGT 6785.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Enumerative Combinatorics
courses.description: Fundamental methods of enumeration and asymptotic analysis, including the use of inclusion/exclusion, generating functions, and recurrence relations. Applications to strings over a finite alphabet and graphs.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Graph Theory
courses.description: Advanced topics in graph theory. Selection of arguments varies every year.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorics
courses.description: Fundamental combinatorial structures including hypergraphs, transversal sets, colorings, Sperner families, intersecting families, packings and coverings, perfect graphs, and Ramsey theory. Algebraic and topological methods, applications.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probabilistic Methods in Combinatorics
courses.description: Applications of probabilistic techniques in discrete mathematics, including classical ideas using expectation and variance as well as modern tools, such as martingale and correlation inequalities.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes and Stochastic Calculus I
courses.description: An introduction to the Ito stochastic calculus and stochastic differential equations through a development of continuous-time martingales and Markov processes. First of two courses.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Processes and Stochastic Calculus II
courses.description: An introduction to the Ito stochastic calculus and stochastic differential equations through a development of continuous-time martingales and Markov processes. Continuation of MATH 7244.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: High-dimensional probability
courses.description: The goal of this PhD level graduate course is to provide a rigorous introduction to the methods of high-dimensional probability.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: High-dimensional statistics
courses.description: The goal of this PhD level graduate course is to provide a rigorous introduction to the methods of high-dimensional statistics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Harmonic Analysis
courses.description: Fourier analysis on the torus and Euclidean space.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Functional Analysis
courses.description: Spectral theory of bounded and unbounded operators, major theorems of functional analysis, additional topics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Analysis
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of advanced material in analysis. This is a Repeatable Course with 5 different subtitles; Recommended prerequisites may vary with each offering.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus of Variations
courses.description: Minimization of functionals, Euler-Lagrange equations, sufficient conditions for a minimum; geodesic, isoperometric, and time of transit problems; variational principles of mechanics; applications to control theory.

courses.subject: MATH

courses.description: Enhancement of English listening/speaking skills for SOM international graduate students, post-docs, and new faculty who speak English as their second language (ESL) and who will be teaching undergraduate students.

courses.description: Application of thermodynamics principles to analysis and design of refrigeration and air conditioning systems, absorption and heat-driven systems, gas-vapor mixture psychrometrics, load estimates, delivery, and control.

courses.description: Technology review and application of engineering sciences and economics to the analysis and design of power generation systems. Fossil, nuclear, and renewable energy systems are considered.

courses.title: Renewable Energy Systems
courses.description: Renewable and efficient energy systems are introduced. Various energy conversion and storage technologies are explained and analyzed, along with their respective advantages and limitations.
courses.prereqGT: Graduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D and Graduate Semester level ME 3340 Minimum Grade of D and Graduate Semester level ME 3345 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Applied Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced study in three areas of fluid mechanics. Topics may be chosen from turbomachinery, flow measurement, compressible flow, applied aerodynamics, and others.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: An introduction to computational fluid dynamics (CFD) in mechanical engineering. The theory and numerical techniques of CFD. Modern CFD software including grid generation and flow visualization tools will be used. Projects with complex fluid-flow systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fundamentals of Mechatronics
courses.description: Focuses on fundamentals of microcontrollers, analog and digital electronics, sensors, actuators and their applications to modern mechatronics systems and intelligent manufacturing. Knowledge gained from lectures will be used to complete lab exercises. Credit will not be awarded for both ME 4405 and ME 6405 or ME 4405 and ME 4777.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3017 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ME 3057 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Mathematical modeling, simulation, and control of robotic systems with mechanical and sensory elements.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3017 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Control of Dynamic Systems
courses.description: Modeling and simulation of dynamic systems in frequency and time domains. Feedback control analysis and design methods including root-locus, frequency response, and pole-placement. Introduction to digital control systems. Credit not allowed for both ME 4452 and ME 3015. Credit not allowed for both ME 4452 and AE 3531.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3017 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3015 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level AE 3515 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Assistantship
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Independent research conducted under the guidance of a faculty member.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wind Engineering
courses.description: An introductory course on wind energy and its potential; modeling and design of wind turbines; analysis of the economic benefits of wind turbine systems. Credit not allowed for both ME 4701 and AE 4701.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2551 or MATH 2561; PHYS 2211 or PHYS 2231.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2401 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2411 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 24X1 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2551 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2561 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X51 Minimum Grade of T) and (Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2231 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Electric Vehicles and the Grid
courses.description: Companies need engineers equipped with skills to drive electrification in their organizations. This course will teach the six E’s of Electrification: EV’s + Ecosystem + Engineering + Energy + Environment + Economics.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 2040 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3710 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Foundations in Machine Learning for Engineers
courses.description: Engineers are taught foundational data analytics principles to learn when, why, and how to use or not use machine learning in engineering problems.
courses.prereqText: ECE 3077 or ISYE 2027; ISYE 2028 or ISYE 3030 or ISYE 3770 or MATH 3670 or BMED 2400; ME 2016.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3077 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2027 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2028 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3030 Minimum Grade of D) or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3770 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3670 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3770 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 2400 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level ME 2016 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CS 4640 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Pulp and Paper Manufacturing
courses.description: The course provides comprehensive foundational knowledge of the industry enabling the student to understand the role of diverse manufacturing operations and to strategically plan improvements. Cross-listed with ChBE 4720.
courses.prereqText: CHBE 2140 (minimum grade C) or ME 3322 or MSE 3001.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2140 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Design
courses.description: Seniors will work in teams to apply a systematic design process to real multi-disciplinary problems. Problems selected from a broad spectrum of interest areas, including biomedical, environmental, mechanical, industrial design, electrical and thermal/fluids. Projects must be based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work, and incorporate appropriate engineering standards and multiple realistic constraints. Emphasis is placed on the design process, the technical aspects of the design, and on reducing the proposed design to practice. The course consists of faculty and guest lectures, prototyping in design studios, and a multi-disciplinary design project.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 2110 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level COE 3001 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ME 3017 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level ME 3180 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 4315 Minimum Grade of D) and Undergraduate Semester level ME 3210 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ME 3345 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ME 3670 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Probabilistic Risk Assessment
courses.description: Introduction to a wide range of probabilistic risk analysis and probabilistic design methods for mechanical systems. Topics covered are probabilistic description, sampling methods, risk assessment, and reliability-based design.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3670 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3770 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Emerging Technologies for Forest Bioproducts
courses.description: The course provides comprehensive knowledge of the manufacture of nontraditional products from forest biomaterials. It analyzes and assesses emerging manufacturing technologies, materials and products. Cross-listed with ChBE 4730.
courses.prereqText: CHBE 2140 (minimum grade C) or ME 3322 or MSE 3001.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2140 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biologically Inspired Design
courses.description: We examine evolutionary adaptation as a source for engineering design inspiration, utilizing principles of scaling, adaptability, and robust multifunctionality that characterize biological systems. Credit not allowed for both ME 4740 and (BIOL 4740, or ISYE 4740 or PTFE 4740 or MSE 4740 ).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1520 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3100 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2231 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Integrative Management Development - Project Preparation
courses.description: Individual and group-based experiential learning activities to develop integrated human system management skills that prepare students for more successful capstone collaboration and learning. Credit not allowed for both ME 4741 and CS 4741 or MGT 4741.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Integrated Technology and Management Capstone Project
courses.description: Project-based course where students in the Technology and Management Program will work in inter-disciplinary teams on projects provided by corporate affiliates. Credit not allowed for both ME 4742 and CS 4742 or MGT 4742.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 4741 Minimum Grade of C

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Global Development Capstone
courses.description: Teams develop solutions to multidisciplinary problems selected from globalization, food security, infrastructure, health, water, sanitation, hygiene, ecosystem resilience, services, capacity building, and urbanization.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level INTA 2050 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Intrapreneurship
courses.description: This course teaches engineering-based Intrapreneurship skills and principles, benefiting students pursuing careers within engineering and innovation driven companies and how to create corporate start-ups.
courses.prereqText: COE 2001 or CHBE 2100 or ECE 2031 or ISYE 2027.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level COE 2001 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2100 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 2031 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 2027 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Topics in Engineering Practice
courses.description: Topics of current inportance offered in collaboration with an approved partner of Georgia Tech's Distance Learning Program.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Electronics Packaging Assembly, Reliability, Thermal Management, and Test
courses.description: The course provides hands-on instruction in electronics packaging, including assembly, reliability, thermal management, and test of next-generation microsystems. Crosslisted with ECE and MSE 4754.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3040 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3710 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biofluid Mechanics
courses.description: Introduction to the study of blood flow in the cardiovascular system. Emphasis on modeling and the potential of flow studies for clinical research application. Crosslisted with AE and CHE 4757.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level AE 2020 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3340 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3300 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CEE 3040 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biosolid Mechanics
courses.description: The mechanics of living tissue, e.g., arteries, skin, heart muscle, ligament, tendon, cartilage, and bone. Constitutive equations and some simple mechanical models. Mechanics of cells. Applications. Crosslisted with AE and CHE 4758.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level COE 3001 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3400 Minimum Grade of D

restrictions.heading: Must be enrolled in one of the following Campuses

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Electrochemical Energy Storage and Conversion
courses.description: An elective class for senior-level students interested in electrochemical storage and conversion, including the fundamentals of electrochemistry and practical battery and fuel cells. Cross-listed with ChBE and MSE 4759.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Acoustics and Noise Control
courses.description: Study of acoustics related to noise and its control; acoustic terminology, wave propagation, wave equation solutions, instrumentation, data processing, room acoustics, noise control, hearing, noise legislation. Crosslisted with AE 4760.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2403 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 24X3 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2413 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2552 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2562 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X52 Minimum Grade of T

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fabrication and Properties of Nanoscale Devices
courses.description: Fundamental properties at the nanoscale for photonics and sensors. Nanoscale fabrication methods including thin films, ion beam, lithography, electroplating, and example case studies in NEMS/MEMS and photonics. Credit not allowed for both ME 4766 and MSE 4766.
courses.prereqText: ME 3322 or ME 3720 or PHYS 3141 or MSE 3001.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3720 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level AE 3450 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 3141 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Pulp and Paper Lab
courses.description: The course offers the fundamentals of pulp and paper testing procedures. Cross-listed with ChBE 4767.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 3130 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering I: Formation and Properties
courses.description: An introduction to the chemistry, structure and formation of polymers, physical states and transitions, physical and mechanical properties of polymer fluids and solids. Crosslisted with CHEM, CHE, MSE, and PTFE 4775.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 2312 or CHEM 1315; CHEM 3411 or MSE 3001 or CHBE 2130 or CHBE 2140 or ME 3322.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 2312 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1315 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 3411 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3001 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2130 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 2140 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3322 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering II: Analysis, Processing, and Laboratory
courses.description: Polymer fabrication processes and methods of characterization and identification of polymers are presented. Experiments in polymerization, processing, and property evaluation of polymers. Crosslisted with CHE, CHEM, MSE, and TFE 4776.
courses.prereqText: CHBE 4775 or CHEM 4775 or ME 4775 or MSE 4775.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 4775 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PTFE 4775 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science and Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to the structure and formation of polymers, physical states and transitions, physical and mechanical properties of polymer fluids and solids, and processing of polymers. Crosslisted with MSE and PTFE 4777.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 2311 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
courses.description: A study of medical instrumentation from a systems viewpoint. Pertinent physiological and electro-physiological concepts will be covered. Credit not allowed for both ME 4781 and (CHE 4781 or CHBE 4781 or BMED 4781 or ECE 4781 ).
courses.prereqText: ECE 3040 (minimum grade C) or ECE 3710 or ECE 3030 (minimum grade C).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3040 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3710 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 3030 Minimum Grade of C

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biosystems Analysis
courses.description: Analytical methods for modeling biological systems, including white-noise protocols for characterizing nonlinear systems. Crosslisted with BMED, CHE and ECE 4782.
courses.prereqText: BMED 3500 or ECE 2040 (minimum grade C) or ME 3017.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3500 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHBE 4400 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ECE 2040 Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3015 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ME 3017 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Materials Selection and Design
courses.description: Principles of selecting materials and processes for engineering applications. Methodologies for designing new materials and conceiving hybrid solutions. Credit not allowed for both ME 4790 and ME 4213 or ME 4790.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level COE 3001 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MSE 3003 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Composites
courses.description: Stress-strain behavior of composites, properties of matrix and reinforcing materials, mechanics of fiber-reinforced composites, lamina and laminate analysis, and mechanical performance. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, MSE, and PTFE 4791.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level COE 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Composite Materials and Processes
courses.description: Basic principles of selection and design of composite materials and their manufacturing and testing. Cost factors. Laboratory exercises on manufacturing and tests. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, ME, MSE, and PTFE 4793.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 1310 or CHEM 1211K or CHEM 1212K; PHYS 2212 or PHYS 2232.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1310 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1211K Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 1212K Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level CHEM 12X1 Minimum Grade of T) and (Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2212 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2232 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fundamental Elements of Nuclear Reactor Materials
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of nuclear reactor materials. Topics covered are basics of radiation damage, defect creation and evolution, microstructure-property correlations in cladding and fuel of nuclear materials.

courses.title: Special Problems
