courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Interfacial Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: The mechanics of fluid interfaces. Mathematical techniques of scaling and calculus of curved surfaces towards analysis of menisci, bubbles, jets, films, foams, and coatings.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Design
courses.description: Design concepts, processes, and methodologies, including quality and robustness. Group project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Designing Open Engineering Systems
courses.description: Decision-based integrated product and process development, meta-design, and decision support problems; mathematical modeling of decisions involving ambiguity and uncertainty; critical thinking and analysis; verification and validation; research issues.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Optimization in Engineering Design
courses.description: Use of single and multi-objective optimization in modeling and solving mechanical engineering design problems. Formulations, solution algorithms, validation and verification, computer implementation. Project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computer-Aided Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of CAD, including geometric and solid modeling, parametric representations, features, and human-machine interactions. Applications to design, analysis, and manufacturing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Modeling and Simulation in Design
courses.description: Modeling and simutaltion concepts, algorithms, and methods; modeling of energy-based and discrete-event systems; modeling of design decisions; information modeling and knowledge representation; project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Finite-Element Method: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Line, plane, solid, plate, and shell elements-theory: practical aspects of modeling; applications in mechanical engineering; final project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Principles of Continuum Mechanics
courses.description: Introductory treatment of the fundamental, unifying concepts of the mechanics of continua.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Inelastic Deformation of Solids
courses.description: Phenomenological aspects of nonlinear material behavior and deformation with emphasis on model development.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Micromechanics of Materials
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of micromechanics of solids with emphasis on application to composite materials.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Manufacturing Processes and Systems
courses.description: Materials processing analysis and selection. Manufacturing systems design. Economic analysis.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Automated Manufacturing Process Planning
courses.description: Fundamentals of process planning. Automated process planning approaches and algorithms. Geometric modeling for process planning. Modeling and analysis of flexible fixturing systems. Mechanical assembly planning.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Machine Tool Analysis and Control
courses.description: Mechanics and dynamics of machining, machine tool components and structures, sensors and control of machine tools, machine process planning and optimization.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Metrology and Measurement Systems
courses.description: Metrology techniques and procedures. Precision manufacturing system design and analysis.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Principles of microfabrication for sensors and actuators. Lumped parameter analysis and computer-aided design; materials properties; case studies include cantilever beam, pressure sensor, and accelerometer.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanics of Contact
courses.description: Mechanics of surface contact, with emphasis on tribological interactions as in rolling element bearings, slider bearings, mechanical seals, and materials processing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fluid Film Lubrication
courses.description: Analytical and numerical investigation of full film compressible and incompressible hydrodynamic lubrication problems for steady and unsteady conditions.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Rotordynamics
courses.description: Analysis and design of shafts for rotating machinery. Torsional vibration, synchronous and nonsynchronous whirl, stability, gyroscopic effects, hydrodynamic bearings, hysteresis, squeeze film dampers, and balancing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanics of Paper Forming and Coating
courses.description: Fundamentals of multiphase flow in paper forming and coating processes, and its impact on the physical properties of composite fiber structure and surface characteristics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Intermediate Heat Transfer
courses.description: Intermediate topics including multidimensional transient conduction, diffusion, boundary layers, internal flows, radiation, phase change, heat exchangers, multimode transfer, and numerical methods with a project-oriented approach.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
courses.description: Steady and transient one- and multi-dimensional conduction. Emphasis on analytical methods, numerical techniques, and approximate solutions.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Convection Heat Transfer
courses.description: Convection (forced and free) in laminar and turbulent, internal and external flows. Analogy between momentum and heat transfer. Scaling laws and modeling.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermal Radiation Heat Transfer
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermal radiation, blackbody radiation, surface characteristics, exchange in enclosures, radiation through continua, and combined mode heat transfer.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Principles of Thermodynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics including energy, entropy, and energy analysis, property relations, equilibrium conditions, and evaluation of properties.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Applications of Thermodynamics
courses.description: Applications of the first and second laws of thermodynamics to analysis and design optimization of power and refrigeration systems incorporating heat exchangers and combustion processes.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Nanoscale Heat Transfer
courses.description: Microscopic concepts and methodology in thermal science, including equilibrium statistics. Boltzmann transport equation, and nano-microscale heat conduction and radiation, with applications in contemporary technologies.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: NUMERICAL HEAT TRANSFER
courses.description: This course will provide foundation to develop numerical solutions for steady state and transient thermal transport problems in complex geometries.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Linear Control Systems
courses.description: Theory and applications of linear systems, state space, stability, feedback controls, observers, LQR, LQG, Kalman filters. Credit will not be awarded for both ME 6401 and AE 6530.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
courses.description: Analysis of nonlinear systems, geometric control, variable structure control, adaptive control, optimal control, applications.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Digital Control Systems
courses.description: Comprehensive treatment of the representation, analysis, and design of discrete-time systems. Techniques include Z- and W- transforms, direct method, control design, and digital tracking.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Control System Design and Implementation
courses.description: Analysis, synthesis, and implementation techniques of continuous-time and real-time control systems using classical and state-space methods.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Mechatronics
courses.description: Modeling and control of actuators and electro-mechanical systems. Performance and application of microprocessors and analog electronics to modern mechatronic systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Machine Vision
courses.description: Design of algorithms for vision systems for manufacturing, farming, construction, and the service industries. Image processing, optics, illumination, feature representation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Analysis and design of robotic systems including arms and vehicles. Kinematics and dynamics. Algorithms for describing, planning, commanding, and controlling motion force.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Mechatronics
courses.description: Focusing on team projects, designing and building intelligent machines and products. Lectures - sensors and transducers, actuators, fluid power, power rectifiers, motion control and modeling of mechatronics systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biomechatronics of Wearable Robotic Devices
courses.description: An introduction to the emerging science of human-machine interaction with particular focus on wearable robotic devices for restoration or augmentation of human movement.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Dynamics of Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Motion analysis and dynamics modeling of systems of particles and rigid bodies in three-dimensional motion.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Vibration of Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Introduction to modeling and oscillatory response analysis for discrete continuous mechanical and structural systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Variational Methods in Engineering
courses.description: Calculus of variations, Hamilton's principle and Lagrange's equations, Sturm-Liouville problems, approximation techniques.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Nonlinear Systems
courses.description: Investigation of nonlinear systems using analytical and numerical techniques.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Acoustic Transducers and Signal Analysis
courses.description: Acoustic instrumentation and methods of signal analysis.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wave Propagation in Solids
courses.description: Wave motion in solids, wave equations, analytical and numerical solutions, ultrasonic NDE.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Microelectromechanical Devices
courses.description: Introduces fundamental concepts and tools needed for the design, simulation and analysis of MEMS devices. These include electrical, mechanical, radiant, thermal, magnetic and chemical domains.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: The fundamentals of fluid mechanics. Derivation of the governing equations of motion. An introduction to viscous, inviscid, turbulent, and boundary-layer flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Viscous Flow
courses.description: The mechanics of Newtonian viscous fluids. The use of modern analytical techniques to obtain solutions for flows with small and large Reynolds numbers.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Interfacial Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: The mechanics of fluid interfaces. Mathematical techniques of scaling and calculus of curved surfaces towards analysis of menisci,bubbles, jets, films, foams, and coatings.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Experimental Methods
courses.description: Experimental methods in mechanics. Includes measurement techniques, instrumentation, data acquisition, signal processing, and linear and digital electronics.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wind Engineering
courses.description: An introductory course on wind energy and its potential; modeling and design of wind turbines; analysis of the economic benefits of wind turbine systems. Credit will not be awarded for both ME 6701 and AE 6701.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Mechatronics
courses.description: Modeling and control of actuators and electro-mechanical systems. Performance and application of microprocessors and analog electronics to modern mechatronic systems.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biotransport
courses.description: This graduate level course covers the analysis of fluid flow phenomena in the human body, cardiovasculature, respiratory system and other organ systems. Credit will not be awarded for both ME 6720 and BMED 6720.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Pulp and Paper Manufacture I
courses.description: The fundamentals of pulp and paper technology are presented. Applications to the several unit operations used are explored and augmented by field trips and recent case studies. Crosslisted with CHE 6741, CHBE 6701 and MLDR 6701.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Biosolid Mechanics
courses.description: Structure-function relationships and constitutive models for a variety of biological tissues, with an emphasis on understanding the mechanical behaviors of normal and pathological tissues. Credit not give for both ME/BMED 6783 and ME/ BMED 6743. Crosslisted with BMED 6743.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Topics in Engineering Practice
courses.description: Topics of current importance offered in collaboration with an approved partner of Georiga Tech's Distance Learning Program. Crosslisted with ECE 6744.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Intrapreneurship
courses.description: This course teaches engineering-based Intrapreneurship skills and principles, benefiting students pursuing careers within engineering and innovation driven companies and how to create corporate start-ups.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Rehabilitation Engineering
courses.description: Students will participate in rehabilitation engineering as practiced in the assistive technology industry. Credit not allowed for both ME 6746 and APPH 6746.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Principles of Management for Engineers
courses.description: The course will provide an introduction to selected topics needed to be successful in the technology industries. Cannot count toward major area requirements on M.S. or Ph.D. programs of study. Crosslisted with MGT 6753.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Acoustics I and II
courses.description: Fundamental principles governing the generation, propagation, reflection, and transmission of sound waves in fluids. Crosslisted with AE 6760.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Acoustics I and II
courses.description: Radiation and scattering of sound waves in fluids, duct acoustics, dissipation phenomena. Crosslisted with AE 6761.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Applied Acoustics
courses.description: Mufflers, resonators, acoustic materials, barriers, industrial noise, room acoustics, active noise control. Crosslisted with AE 6762.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Kinetics and Thermodynamics of Gases
courses.description: Thermodynamics of nonreacting and reacting gas mixtures. Introductory quantum theory, statistical thermodynamics, and gas kinetic theory. Crosslisted with AE 6765.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Combustion I
courses.description: Introductory chemical kinetics, deformations and deflagrations, laminar flame propagation in premixed gases, ignition and quenching, laminar diffusion flames, droplet burning, and turbulent reacting flows. Crosslisted with AE 6766.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Polymer Structure, Physical Properties, and Characterization
courses.description: Formulations and analysis of molecular and phenomenological models of elastic and viscoelastic behavior, development and description of structure, and fundamental aspects of structure-property relations. Crosslisted with CHE, MSE, and PTFE 6768.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Linear Elasticity
courses.description: Governing equations of linear elasticity, plane elasticity, boundary-value problems, airy stress function and complex variable methods, simple three-dimensional solutions. Crosslisted with AE 6769.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Energy and Variational Methods in Elasticity and Plasticity
courses.description: Applications in energy and variational methods in engineering mechanics to elastic, plastic, and dynamical behavior of deformable media. Crosslisted with AE 6770.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Integrated Low-cost Microelectronics Systems Packaging
courses.description: Broad overview of system-level, cross-disciplinary microelectronics packaging technologies, including design, test, thermal, reliability, optoelectronics, and RF integration. Comparison of system-on-chip and system-on-package. Crosslisted with ECE and MSE 6776.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Biomaterials
courses.description: Advanced topics of biomaterials performance and engineering, including biointerfaces, host reactions to materials, and bio-inspired/smart-materials strategies. Crosslisted with BMED, CHE, and MSE 6777.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermal Engineering for Packaging of Micro and Nano Systems
courses.description: Passive, active, and hybrid thermal management techniques, and computational modeling of micro systems. Air cooling, single phase and phase change liquid cooling, heat pipes, and thermoelectrics. Crosslisted with ECE 6779.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Cellular Engineering
courses.description: Engineering analysis of cellular systems. Crosslisted with BMED and CHE 6782.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Technology Ventures
courses.description: Team discussion and case studies of issues in biomedical engineering technology transfer including licensing, financial capital, safety and efficacy studies, clinical trials, and strategic planning. Crosslisted with BMED, ECE, CHE, and MGT 6789.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computer Integrated Manufacturing Systems Seminar
courses.description: Guest speakers on a broad range of manufacturing-related topics: research, applications, and technology. Required for Certificate in Manufacturing. Crosslisted with ECE and ISYE 6792.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Systems Pathophysiology
courses.description: Overview of human pathophysiology from a quantitative perspective. Emphasis on systems of interest to bioengineering faculty. Introduction to quantitative models for biological systems. Crosslisted with BMED, CHE, and ECE 6793.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Tissue Engineering
courses.description: Biological, engineering, and medical issues in developing tissue-engineered constructs. Emphasis in the integration of these disciplines at a basic molecular and cell biology level. Crosslisted with BMED and CHE 6794.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mathematical, Statistical, and Computational Techniques in Materials Science
courses.description: Emphasizes the fundamental physical, analytical, and mathematical techniques commonly encountered in materials engineering including stress and strain, crystallographic and orientation transformations, X-ray, TEM, and solid-state concepts. Crosslisted with MSE and PTFE 6795.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Structure-Property Relationships in Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the multi-scale structure effects on material properties. For MSE students, this course will prepare students for future in-depth courses. For non-MSE students, the course will provide a background in materials and may serve as part of the program of study for a minor in materials. Crosslisted with MSE and PTFE 6796.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Microstructural Evolution
courses.description: The reduction of chemical-free energy, strain energy, and interfacial energy controls the kinetics of diffusional transformations. These factors are explored from the point of view of processing and stability of the microstructure during service. Crosslisted with MSE and PTFE 6797.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Legal Issues in Technology Transfer
courses.description: Study and analysis of U.S. law as it applies to the patenting and licensing processes. Crosslisted with CHE, MGT, and BMED 6799.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: GT-STUTTGART
courses.description: Placeholder for GT-STUTTGART students.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: GT-SEOUL
courses.description: Placeholder for GT-SEOUL students.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Computational treatments of material and geometric nonlinearity, with emphasis on rate-dependent elasto-plasticity and fracture.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Constitutive Relations for Solids
courses.description: Advanced treatment of constitutive laws for nonlinear behavior of solids. Coupled thermomechanical laws and underlying physical and thermodynamical bases. Behavior of media with underlying substructure.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanics and Applications of Nanostructured Materials and Devices
courses.description: Introduction to mechanics and transport processes of discrete atomistic and molecular systems, fabrication of nanodevices/structures and applications to nanoelectronics, tribology, actuation and sensors.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Additive Manufacturing and Rapid Prototyping
courses.description: Rapid prototyping technologies in engineering design. Physical principles, materials, materials processing. Laboratory demonstrations and project.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Transport Phenomena in Multiphase Flow
courses.description: Gas-liquid, two-phase flow patterns, basic and empirical models; conservation equations and closure relations; pool and convective boiling; aerosol transport; condensation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Vibration of Continuous Systems
courses.description: Equations of motion and oscillatory response of dynamic systems modeled as continuous media.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Hydrodynamic Stability
courses.description: Hydrodynamic stability of fluid flows using linear, energy, and nonlinear stability theories. Taylor-Couette, buoyancy- driven, surface-tension-driven, shear, and thin-film flows.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robotics Professional Preparation
courses.description: Preparation for a professional career in Robotics. Local & visiting speakers. Program introduction. Technical resume preparation. GT Robotics labs & resources.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robotics Professional Preparation 2
courses.description: Preparation for a professional career in Robotics. Local & visiting speakers. Selecting and applying for Internship. Developing capstone project proposal. Public speaking practice and preparation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Robotics Professional Preparation 3
courses.description: Preparation for a professional career in Robotics. Local & visiting speakers. Interview preparation & career search. Technical report writing and presentation.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Numerical methods for solving the time-dependent Navier-Stokes equations in complex geometrics, including theory, implementation, and applications. Crosslisted with CEE 7751.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Supervised teaching for doctoral students. Teaching techniques, course and curriculum design, student evaluation methods and criteria. Students may, in some instances, prepare and present lectures. Crosslisted with NRE, HP, and CHBE 7757.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Acoustic Propagation
courses.description: Propagation of sound in inhomogeneous fluids; ray acoustics, ocean and atmospheric acoustics, nonlinear acoustics. Crosslisted with AE 7764.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechanics of Polymer Solids and Fluids
courses.description: Continuum mechanics of solids and fluids; mechanics of deformation of anisotropic polymers; yield, breaking, and fatigue; non-Newtonian viscous and viscoelastic behavior of polymer fluids. Crosslisted with CHE, MSE, and PTFE 7771.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fundamentals of Fracture Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced study of failure of structural materials under load, mechanics of fracture, and microscopic and macroscopic aspects of the fracture of engineering materials. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and MSE 7772.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Fracture Mechanics
courses.description: Nonlinear fracture mechanics including elastic-plastic and time-dependent fracture, advanced test methods, J-integral theory, and extensions. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and MSE 7773.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fatigue of Materials and Structures
courses.description: Mechanical and microstructural aspects of nucleation and growth of cracks under cyclic loading conditions, notch effects, cumulative damage, multiaxial loading, and fatigue crack propagation. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, and MSE 7774.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Topics in Fracture and Fatigue of Metallic and Composite Structures
courses.description: Brittle and ductile failure criteria. Failure prediction in composite structures. Free-edge and internal delamination. Anisotropic cracks. Fatigue behavior of composites and comparison with metal fatigue. Crosslisted with AE, CHE, and MSE 7775.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Introduction to Robotics Research
courses.description: Familiarizes students with the core areas of robotics; mechanics, control, perception, AI, and autonomy. Provides an introduction to the mathematical tools required in robotics research.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Manufacturing of Composites
courses.description: Major manufacturing techniques of metal-ceramic and polymer-matrix composites. Modeling of processes with emphasis on fundamental mechanisms and effects. Crosslisted with AE, CEE, CHE, MSE, and PTFE 7793.

courses.title: Radiation Therapy Physics
courses.description: Clinical radiation oncology, phantom systems, radiation machines, photon beams, electron beams, brachythearpy, dose modeling and treatment planning.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiation Therapy Treatment Planning Laboratory
courses.description: Radiation therapy treatment planning course covering conventional radiation therapy treatment planning, monitor unit calculations, and advanced radiation treatment planning techniques.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiation Therapy Physics
courses.description: Measurement and calculation of absorbed dose, dose distributions, treatment planning, photon teletherapy, electron teletherapy, brachytherapy, clinical linear accelerators, quality assurance.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiological Anatomy
courses.description: A survey of the most clinically relevant anatomy as visualized by modern diagnostic imaging; plan radiographs, CT, MRI, and PET are emphasized.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Medical Health Physics
courses.description: Basics of medical health physics, Title 10, U.S. Code of Federal Regulations, Parts 19, 20 and 35, shielding for hospital radiation facilities.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiation Dosimetry
courses.description: Dosimetry of ionizing radiation: photons, neutrons, and charged particles; cavity theory; concept of exposure and absorbed dose; ion chambers and other types of integration dosimeters.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Applications of the Monte Carlo Method in Medical Physics
courses.description: Basic principles of the Monte Carlo method, Monte Carlo transport of photon and electron, various applications of the Monte Carlo method in medical physics.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiation Dosimetry & Protection
courses.description: Introduction to the calculation of radiation dose, dosimetry, and health physics.

courses.subject: MP
courses.title: Radiation Biology and Oncology
courses.description: Radiation lesions and repair, mechanisms of cell death, cell cycle effect, radiation sensitizers and protectors, tumor radiobiology, relative sensitivities of human tissues, and radiation carcinogenesis.

courses.title: Radiation Physics
courses.description: Characteristics of atomic and nuclear radiation, transition probabilities, radioactivity abd isotopes, cross sections, electromagnetic radiation, neutrons, and charges particle interaction with matter. Crosslisted with NRE 6756 and HP 6756.

courses.subject: MP

courses.description: Introduction to the theory and application of radiation detectors, measurement methods, signal processing, and data analysis. Crosslisted with HP 6757 and NRE 6757.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership and Personal Development
courses.description: Introduces cadets to the personal challenges and compentencies that are critical for effective leadership. Cadets learn how the personal development of life skills such as critical thinking, goal setting, time management, physical fitness, and stress management relate to leadership, officership, and the Army profession. The focus is on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of Army leadership dimensions while gaining a big picture understanding of the ROTC program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Introduction to Tactical Leadership
courses.description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feed-back, and using elective writing skills. Cadets explore dimensions of leadership values, attributes, skills and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Continued emphasis is placed on recruitment and retention of cadets. Cadre role models and the building of stronger relationships among the cadets through common exercise and practical interaction are critical aspects of this course.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 1001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Innovative Team Leadership
courses.description: Explores the dimensions of creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles by examining team dynamics and two historical leadership theories that form the basis of the Army leadership framework (trait and behavior theories). Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building in the context of planning, executing, and assessing team exercises and participating in leadership labs. Focus is on continued development of the knowledge of leadership values and attributes through an understanding of Army rank, structure, duties and basic aspects of land navigation and squad tactics. Case studies provide tangible context for learning the Soldier's Creed and Warrior Ethos as they apply in the contemporary operating environment (COE).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 1002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Foundations of Tactical Leadership
courses.description: Examines the challenges of leading tactical teams in the complex contemporary operating environment (COE). The course highlights dimensions of terrain analysis, patrolling, and operation orders. Further study of the theoretical basis of the Army leadership framework explores the dynamics of adaptive leadership in the context of military operations. Cadets develop greater self awareness as they assess their own leadership styles ad practice communication and team building skills. COE case studies give insight into the importance and practice of teamwork and tactics in real-world scenarios.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Adaptive Tactical Leadership
courses.description: Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills as they are presented with challenging scenarios related to squad tactical operations. Cadets receive systematic and specific feedback on their leadership attributes and actions. Based on such feedback, as well as their own self evaluations, cadets continue to develop their leadership and critical thinking abilities. The focus is developing cadets' tatical leadership abilities to enable them to succeed at ROTC's summer Leadership Development and Assessment Course (LDAC).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 2002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership in Changing Environments
courses.description: Uses increasingly intense situational leadership challenges to build cadet awareness and skills in leading tactical operations up to platoon level. Cadets review aspects of combat, stability, and support operations. They also conduct military briefings and develop proficiency in garrison operation orders. The focus is on exploring, evaluating, and developing skills in decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members in the contemporary operating environment (COE). Cadets are evaluated on what they know, and do as leaders as they prepare to attend the ROTC summer Leadership Develpment Assessment Course (LDAC).
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 3001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Developing Adaptive Leaders
courses.description: Develops cadet proficiency in planning, executing, and assessing complex operations, funtioning as a member of a staff, and providing performance feedback to subordinates. Cadets assess risk, make ethical decisions, and lead fellow ROTC cadets. Lessons on military justice and personnel processes prepare cadets to make the transition to Army officers. MSIV cadets analyze, evaluate, and instruct cadets at lower levels. Both their classroom and battalion leadership experiences are designed to prepare cades for their first unit of assignment. They identify responsibilities of key staff, coordinate staff roles, and use situational opportunitites to teach, train, and develop subordinates.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 3002 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership in a Complex World
courses.description: Explores the dynamics of leading in the complex situations of current military operations in the contemporary operating environment (COE). Cadets examine differences in customes and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism. They also explore aspects of interacting with non-government organizations, civilians on the battlefield, and host national support. The course places significant emphasis on preparing cadets for their first unit of assignment. It uses case studies, scenarios, and "What now Lieutenant?" exercises to prepare cadets to face the complex ethical and practical demands of leading as commissioned officers in the United States Army.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSL 4001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE

courses.description: Introduction to experimental nuclear reactor physics techniques including criticality, flux mapping, buckling measurements, subcritical assembly measurements, diffusion length measurement, neutron spectral measurements, and foil activation methods.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3208 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3112 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Radiation Detection
courses.description: An introduction to the principles and characteristics of basic detectors for nuclear radiation and the pulse processing electronics associated with them.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Physics
courses.description: Characteristics of atomic and nuclear radiations, transition probabilities, radioactivity, classical and quantum-mechanical derivations of cross sections, interactions of photon, neutron, and charged particles with matter.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1502 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1512 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 15X2 Minimum Grade of T or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1552 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1X52 Minimum Grade of T) and (Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2231 Minimum Grade of D) and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 2120 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Protection Engineering
courses.description: Covers radiation dosimetry, biological effects of radiation, radiation-protection criteria and exposure limits, external radiation protection, internal radiation protection, and sources of human exposure.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2403 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2413 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 24X3 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2552 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2562 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2X52 Minimum Grade of T) and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3301 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Reactor Theory
courses.description: Students will learn physical nuclear reactor concepts, nuclear data and computational methodology required to understand the design process of nuclear fission reactors.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 2552 Minimum Grade of C and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3208 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Reactor Engineering
courses.description: Nuclear heat generation; fuel elements' thermal analysis; single and two-phase flow and heat transfer in reactor systems; core thermal design and treatment of uncertainties.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level ME 3345 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3208 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Criticality Safety Engineering
courses.description: This course covers the theoretical concepts, the computational techniques, and the principal methods of criticality safety.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 4204 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Light Water Reactor Technology
courses.description: A systematic survey of the technology of both pressurized and boiling water reactors with emphasis on the nuclear stream supply system and its associated safety and control systems.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3208 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Sources and Applications
courses.description: Radiation Sources. Radioisotope production. Application of radiation and radioisotope technology in industry and medicine.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3316 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Design Methods & Tools
courses.description: Introduction to selected methods and nuclear engineering analytic tools (computer codes) with tutorials.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3208 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3316 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Design of Nuclear and Radiological Systems
courses.description: NRE Capstone Design course - an open-minded design project, performed by students organized in design teams, that integrates all relevant nuclear and radiological engineering aspects.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 4350 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level NRE 4214 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level NRE 4328 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiological Assessment and Waste Management
courses.description: Mathematical models for movement in the environment. Scenario development for release, environmental transport, and exposure. Radioactive waste disposal facilities and waste disposal technology.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3316 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Introduction to Radiobiology and Oncology
courses.description: This course will provide the student with a basic knowledge of radiation biology as it pertains to oncology and radiotherapy.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3301 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Regulatory Requirements
courses.description: This course introduces regulatory organizations and delineates their jurisdictions. It covers the fundamentals of regulations, the impacts on occupational workers, the public, and the environment.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3316 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Introduction to Plasma Physics and Fusion Engineering
courses.description: A first course in plasma physics and magnetic confinement fusion: basic plasma physics, magnetic confinement concepts, fusion engineering, and a review of the current status of fusion research.

courses.subject: NRE

courses.description: Introduction to a wide range of probabilistic risk analysis and probabilistic design methods for mechanical systems. Topics covered are probabilistic description, sampling methods, risk assessment, and reliability-based design.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 3670 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level ISYE 3770 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Diagnostic Imaging Physics
courses.description: Physics and image formation methods for conventional X-ray CT, nuclear medicine, and magnetic resonance and ultrasound imaging.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level NRE 3112 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Chemical Engineering
courses.description: This course surveys the chemical engineering aspects of nuclear power. Topics include nuclear reactions, fuel cycles, solvent extraction of metals, the properties of actinides and other irradiated fuel materials, fuel reprocessing, and radioactive waste management. Crosslisted with CHBE 4770.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Fundamental Elements of Nuclear Reactor Materials
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of nuclear reactor materials. Topics covered are basics of radiation damage, defect creation and evolution, microstructure-property correlations in cladding and fuel of nuclear materials.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MSE 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Transport Fundamentals
courses.description: Neutral and charged particle transport. Fluid mass, energy, and momentum transport. Models used in nuclear radiation transport; fluid hydrodynamics, radiative and plasma transport.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Plasma Physics
courses.description: Physics of ionized plasmas. Magnetic confinement, kinetic and fluid theories, equilibrium, waves and stability, plasma-material interactions, atomic/molecular-plasma interactions, multispecies transport. Plasma processing applications.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Computational Methods of Radiation Transport
courses.description: Deterministic and stochastic computational methods for solving transport equations of neutral particles.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Reactor Physics
courses.description: Fundamentals of reactor physics for nuclear analysis of neutron chain reactors and for developing tools required for design of those reactors.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Reactor Engineering
courses.description: Two-phase flow, boiling heat transfer, fast reactor thermal-hydraulics, reactor thermal-hydraulics uncertainty analysis, loss-of-coolant accidents. Reactor thermal- hydraulic accident analysis.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Advanced Nuclear Engineering Design
courses.description: Synthesis of principles of nuclear engineering in the design of nuclear reactors and other facilities.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Criticality Safety Engineering
courses.description: Concepts, computational techniques, and the principal methods of criticality safety such as accident experience, standards, experiments, computer and hand calculations, limits and regulations. Application to overall facility operation.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Fuel Cycle
courses.description: Fission fuel cycle, uranium mining and milling, enrichment. Fuel fabrication. In-core fuel management. Reprocessing and fuel cycle economics. Spent-fuel waste management.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Nuclear Materials
courses.description: Materials science and engineering of metallic and ceramic fuels; cladding, structural, and control materials including radiation effects.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Management of the Nuclear Enterprise
courses.description: Identify and understand the unique challenges of and techniques for managing highly technical, potentially hazardous operations, issues within the nuclear industry.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Nuclear Nonproliferation
courses.description: This course explores the fundamentals of nuclear energy generation, pathways of materials misuse, the implication of nuclear technology for international security and policy.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Seminar: Politics Tech & Proliferation
courses.description: This seminar course is designed specifically to encourage new thinking and creative effort on nuclear deterrence and strategic stability for our global future.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiological Assessment and Waste Management
courses.description: Critical analyses of sources and human exposures, mathematical models for movement through the biosphere, environmental transport, and exposure for nuclear facilities and waste disposal processing. Crosslisted with HP 6755.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Physics
courses.description: Characteristics of atomic and nuclear radiation, transition probabilities, radioactivity and isotopes, cross sections, electromagnetic radiation, neutrons, and charged particle interaction with matter. Crosslisted with HP 6756.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Detection
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and application of radiation detectors, measurement methods, signal processing, and data analysis. Crosslisted with HP 6757.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Numerical methods for solution of engineering problems; initial, eigenvalue, and boundary-value problems; computational stability for ordinary and linear partial differential equations. Crosslisted with ME and HP 6758.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Radiation Shielding Principles and Analysis
courses.description: Principles of Radiation Shielding; Design of Shields; Computational Methods for Analysis of Shielding; Emphasis on Monte Carlo Simulation as a Shielding Tool.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Advanced Plasma Physics
courses.description: Classical and collective transport phenomena, plasma instabilities, plasma-materials interactions, and plasma edge physics. Emphasis on magnetic fusion, plasma processing, and other plasma applications research.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Advanced Reactor Physics
courses.description: Advanced topics in reactor physics and transport theory.

courses.subject: NRE
courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Supervised teaching for doctoral students. Teaching techniques, course and curriculum design, student evaluation methods and criteria. Students may, in some instances, prepare and present lectures. Crosslisted with HP, ME, and CHBE 7757.

courses.subject: NRE

courses.description: Seminars involving current research projects presented by graduate students, faculty, and invited speakers.

courses.subject: PERS

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophical Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to the nature of philosophy through the critical analysis of selected works, such as Descartes, Hobbes, and Locke. The relationship of philosophy to science, religion, and culture will be emphasized. Credit not allowed for both PST 1101 and PHIL 2010.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Analysis of Policy Choices
courses.description: An introduction to philosophical questions that may arise in public policy debate and decision making and to resources from the philosophical tradition for addressing them. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 2025 and PST 2020 or PHIL 2025 and PST 2068.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Political Philosophy
courses.description: An exploration of the main currents in political philosophy from antiquity to the present, seeking resources for analyzing contemporary debates about policy and political process. Credit not allowed for both PST 3050 and PHIL 3050.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: AI Ethics and Policy
courses.description: This course explores the ethical and philosophical dimensions of artificial intelligence, and it examines policies that can, or should, govern its development and use.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ancient Philosophy
courses.description: Development of philosophy in the classical works of Ancient Greek philosophy. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3102 and PST 3102.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Modern Philosophy
courses.description: A study of the development of philosophy from the views of Bacon and Descartes to the beginning of the 20th century. Traces the philosophic response to modern science in the rational and empirical traditions. Credit not allowed for both PST 3103 and PHIL 3103.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethical Theories
courses.description: Surveys traditional ethical theories of value, obligation, and rights and applies these theories to contemporary social problems such as abortion, euthanasia, poverty, and distributional equity, and environmental problems. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3105 and PST 3105.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Engineering Ethics
courses.description: Ethical reasoning in the context of professional work in science and technology. Prepares future technical professionals to approach decision with a coherent ethical framework. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3109 and PST 3109.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Logic and Critical Thinking
courses.description: Symbolic logic and applications of logic in critical reading and thinking by exploring modern systems of symbolic logic and their implications for science. Emphasizes skills in critical thinking and writing based on the principles of logic. Credit not allowed for both PST 3113 and PHIL 3113.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.description: Examination of the nature and processes of scientific inquiry, including the status of scientific knowledge, identification of pseudoscientific claims, and the role of values in generating and using scientific knowledge. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3115 and PST 3115.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Human Values
courses.description: Exploration of the boundaries between science, religion, and social values, examining science and technology in a broader social context. Examines claims that science is isolated from social problems and values. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3127 and PST 3127.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Technology
courses.description: The course considers philosophical accounts of how technologies can and should shape our understandings of politics, ethics, and daily life.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Food
courses.description: Examines a range of philosophical and political issues pertaining to the production and consumption of food.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.description: A survey of major issues in contemporary biomedical ethics, using well-constructed arguments to understand basic controversies in medicine, research, end-of-life care, and other topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
courses.description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on cognitive science. Interdisciplinary approaches to issues in cognition, including memory, language, problem solving, learning, perception, and action. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 3790 and PST 3790 (or CS 3790, PSYC 3790, ISYE 3790 ).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Theories of Knowledge
courses.description: Critical examination of perception, verification, apriori and aposteriori knowledge, meaning and criteria of truth, and cognitive significance of scientific and philosophical propositions. Evolution of epistemology. Credit not allowed for both PHIL 4110 and PST 4110.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics I
courses.description: An introductory course which will include mechanics (kinematics, dynamics, work and energy, momentum and collisions, and rotational motion and statics), and will include thermodynamics and waves. Elementary algebra and trigonometry will be used.

courses.subject: PHYS

courses.description: This course covers Ancient and Renaissance astronomy, gravity, sky phenomena, telescopes, and the solar system.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Stars, Galaxies, and the Universe
courses.description: This course covers optics, telescopes, stellar characteristics and evolution, galaxies, the universe, and the big bang. Physics topics include mechanics, optics, atomic physics, nuclear physics, and relativity.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Astrophysics
courses.description: This course provides an overview of modern astrophysics including stars, galaxies, black holes and other dense stellar remnants, and the physics of the expanding Universe.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Principles of Physics I
courses.description: An introductory course which will include mechanics (kinematics, dynamics, work and energy, momentum and collisions, and rotational motion and statics), and may also include oscillations and computational methods. This is a calculus-based course.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1552 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1555 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1X52 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 15X2 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Principles of Physics II
courses.description: An introductory course which will include electrostatics, electric current and circuits, electromagnetism, and may also include light and computational methods. This is a calculus-based course.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2231 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Physics
courses.description: A survey of twentieth century physics. Developments of several branches of physics up to their present frontiers, including historical and philosophical perspectives.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2212 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2232 Minimum Grade of D

courses.description: Parallels introductory Physics I ( PHYS 2211 ). Some topics treated in more depth or more extensively. A rigorous physics foundation requiring demonstrated competence in mathematics.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1502 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1512 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MATH 1552 Minimum Grade of D

courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2211 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PHYS 2231 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Vibrations and Waves
courses.description: An introduction to oscillating and wave systems in physics, illustrated with examples drawn from different physical settings (e.g., mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics).
courses.prereqText: PHYS 2211 or PHYS 2231; PHYS 2212 or PHYS 2232; MATH 2551.

courses.description: A first course in special relativity and quantum physics, including both fundamental concepts (e.g., wave-particle duality) and applications (e.g., radioactivity). Credit not awarded for both PHYS 2304 and PHYS 2213.

courses.title: Electromagnetism
courses.description: An advanced treatment of electromagnetism. Topics include boundary value problems in electrostatics and magnetostatics, Maxwell’s equations, and radiation from charged particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism II
courses.description: Theory of generation of electromagnetic waves, their propagation, scattering, and diffraction. Covariant formulation of electrodynamics and application to radiation from charged particles.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description: An axiomatic development of quantum mechanics. Topics include linear vector spaces, linear operators, infinitesimal transformations, function space, representation and transformation groups.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description: Applications of quantum mechanics. Topics include systems with spin and angular momentum, atomic structure, time-dependent phenomena, scattering, and various methods of modeling and approximations.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics I
courses.description: Equilibrium statistical mechanics for closed and open systems. Probability distribution for classical and quantum systems. Partition functions and associated thermodynamical potentials.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical Methods of Physics I
courses.description: First of two courses on mathematical methods used in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, and statistical physics. Topics include complex analysis, vectors and matrices, and Sturm-Liouville theory.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Soft Matter Physics
courses.description: Introduction to the properties and physical description of soft matter systems including polymers, colloids and interfaces.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics I
courses.description: Introduction to condensed matter physics. Crystal structure, electronic and thermal properties, response to external electric and magnetic fields.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics II
courses.description: Collective and many-electron properties in condensed matter systems. Topics include second quantization, magnetism, phase transitions, and superconductivity.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astrophysical Radiative Processes
courses.description: Radiation emission, absorption and scattering processes in astrophysical systems, including bremsstrahlung and synchrotron radiation. An introduction to radiation transfer. Determining physical quantities from observations.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics
courses.description: Introduction to physical concepts connect to the workings of biological systems at a molecular level. Topics include polymer theory of proteins, diffusion, and bioelectricity.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics
courses.description: Applications of numerical methods and computer programming to condensed matter; astrophysical hydrodynamics, gravitational physics, black holes and cosmology.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Data Science for Physicists
courses.description: Introduction to probability theory, classical statistics and machine learning, and their application to physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Atomic Physics I
courses.description: This course provides a detailed description of atomic structures and interactions. It contains applications of advanced quantum mechanics to problems in modern atomic physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
courses.description: A modern introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Topics include driven oscillators, entrainment, bifurcation, fractals, and control of chaos. Examples are drawn from physical systems.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Ultrafast Optics
courses.description: A modern introduction to ultrafast optical phenomena. Topics include the generation, amplification, measurement, nonlinear optics, propagation, focusing, shaping and applications of ultrashort laser pulses.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Estimation and Approximation in Physics
courses.description: Applications of order-of-magnitude estimates, dimensional analysis, scaling arguments, and perturbation theory in different areas of physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Foundations of Quantitative Biosciences
courses.description: Introduction to quantitative methods and logic that enable key advances in understanding living systems, spanning molecules, cells, organisms, and biomes.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Space Plasma Physics
courses.description: This course will cover theoretical concepts in space plasma physics as well as observations of these phenomena by past and ongoing spacecraft missions.

courses.subject: PHYS

courses.description: Optoelectronic materials, physical processes, and devices. Includes compound semiconductor materials, excitation, recombination, gain, and modulation processes, and devices such as emitters, detectors, and modulators. Crosslisted with ECE 6771.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Grant Writing and Navigating the Scientific Landscape
courses.description: An introduction to the skills of a professional scientist both within academia and beyond, focusing on preparing grants and proposals, scientific communication and career preparation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics GTA Preparation
courses.description: An introduction to learner-centered teaching methods and best practices for new physics graduate teaching assistants.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics II
courses.description: Principles of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, both classical and quantal. Emphasis is on the dynamics of fluctuations, their measurement, and their relationship to transport properties.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Relativity
courses.description: The theory of gravity, describing how matter curves spacetime and spacetime guides matter, with its experimental and theoretical applications.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Cosmology & Galaxies
courses.description: Overview of the relevant physics that govern cosmological processes, and galaxy formation and evolution. Topics include inflation, gravitational collapse, large-scale clustering, and galaxy mergers.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High-Energy Astrophysics
courses.description: Introduction to high-energy astrophysical processes and environments, including astrophysical fluid dynamics (e.g., shocks and blast waves), accretion onto compact objects, and clusters of galaxies.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Many-Particle Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Quantum mechanics of interacting Fermi and Bose particles. Topics include second quantization, diagrammatic purturbation theory, variational methods, and path integrals.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Group Theory and Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Foundations of group representation theory with applications in atomic, molecular, nuclear, and solid state physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Field Theory
courses.description: Introduction to quantum field theory, with an emphasis in quantum electrodynamics. Second quantization, Dirac equation, Feynman diagrams, quantum electrodynamics, electro-weak interactions.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Optics I
courses.description: Basic course on the interaction of light with matter, based on quantum theory. Applications to the laser and to the study of coherence properties of light.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonlinear Hamiltonian Dynamics and Chaos
courses.description: A course on nonlinear dissipative dynamical systems, with an emphasis in aspects relevant to physicists. Topics include bifurcation theory, attractors, renormalization group techniques, and pattern formation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics and Pattern Formation
courses.description: A theoretical description of dynamics and pattern formation in physical, chemical and biological systems driven out of equilibrium. Topics include linear and weakly nonlinear analysis of patterns, bifurcation theory and amplitude equations.

courses.description: Introduction to political models and theories of policy making. Agenda-setting, stakeholder involvement, policy adoption, policy design and implementation, evaluation, and advocacy.

courses.title: Foundations of Public Policy
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of American public policy, with emphasis on the dynamics of policymaking in policy areas such as health care, research, energy and environment, income maintenance, and economic development.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Organizations and Policy
courses.description: An exploration of the roles and activities of bureaucracies in the implementation of policies and programs, with emphasis on practical issues of public management. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 2030 and PUBP 3010.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Teams and Collaboration in Context

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: American Constitutional Issues
courses.description: Examines the American social and political system through the prism of Constitutional issues decided by the U.S. Supreme Court. Includes study of the Constitution of Georgia.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Judicial Process
courses.description: The functions, structures, and procedures of state and federal court systems, including selection and appointment of judges, judicial activism, influences on court decisions, and enforcement of court decisions.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Applied Political Economy
courses.description: Roles of markets and government in allocating resources. Rational choice approaches to understanding policy. Institutional design. Growth and sustainability.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 2010 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 2030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ECON 2106 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Policy Analysis
courses.description: The science and craft of professional problem-solving, analysis, and advice. Economic and political approaches and techniques for analysis of costs, benefits, and risks.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 2010 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 2030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level ECON 2106 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Data Science for Public Policy
courses.description: Introduces fundamentals of data science, tools, and quantitative methodologies and ethical implications for public and social applications. Topics for policy applications vary by semester.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Statistical Analysis for Public Policy
courses.description: Introduction to probability, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics and analysis, and spreadsheets. Emphasis application of basic statistical concepts to public policy and administration problems. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 3120 and PUBP 4113.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Research Methods and Problem Solving
courses.description: Conceptual and methodological issues in policy studies, including causality, explanation, models, threats to research, data collection, and assessment of applicability to policy issues. Design of research. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 3130 and PUBP 3110.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Leading Social Organizations
courses.description: This course is designed to give the student a sound understanding of how to lead and manage change in social organizations.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Introduction to Social Policy
courses.description: A survey of public policies directed toward social problems in America and their evolution and reform. Development of role of government in addressing issues related to poverty and social welfare.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: U.S. Health Policy
courses.description: Evolution of major US health care institutions and related policies and politics; their purposes, effects, and relationships; and recent and possible health policy reforms.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: African American Politics
courses.description: An exploration of the organizations, strategies, and issues that have defined African American political life in the post-civil rights era in the United States.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: STEM Education Policy
courses.description: A seminar exploring the role of public policy in shaping the conduct of STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) education in the United States.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Stem Cell Science, Policy, and Ethics
courses.description: Examination of current state of scientific knowledge regarding stem cells and historical development, relevant ethical issues, and policy considerations.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Environmental Policy and Politics
courses.description: Overview of the major institutions, organizations, official and unofficial actors in environmental policy and politics, and what influences their environmental decisions and actions. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 3315 and PUBP 4314.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level POL 1101 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level INTA 1200 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Climate Policy
courses.description: Examines relevant scientific theory and evidence, political history, policy options, alternative policy analysis frameworks, and the influence of science and scientific uncertainity on climate policy.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.description: Examines policies impacting the production and utilization of energy in the U.S. and abroad. Addresses resource constraints, physical principles, and policy analysis tools and concepts.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Information and Communications Technology Policy
courses.description: Examination of the convergence of information technology, communications and telecommunications, policymaking within the executive/regulatory branches, special interest group role, and key domestic and international issues. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 3502 and PUBP 4512.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Politics and Policy
courses.description: Application of political science and other social science concepts and theories to current issues. Investigates several current topics in detail.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Globalization and Public Policy
courses.description: This course will serve as an introduction to the fundamental concepts, theories, conflicts, and issues of globalization and its effects on public policy.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Sustainability, Technology, and Policy
courses.description: Ethical, scientific, technological, economic, and political dimensions of sustainable human practices, applying multidisciplinary perspectives to challenges facing public and private-sector approaches to sustainability.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Pre-Law Seminar
courses.description: Examination of the legal profession and areas of legal specialization (e.g., contract, property, intellectual property, international). Emphasizes skills and values that are essential to success in law school and competent lawyering.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Policy Task Force I
courses.description: Capstone project in which teams of students formulate, analyze, and recommend policy options.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3030 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3130 Minimum Grade of D and (Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3120 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level MGT 2250 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Policy Task Force II
courses.description: Capstone project in which teams of students formulate, analyze, and recommend policy options.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 4010 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level MGT 2250 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3120 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Internet and Public Policy
courses.description: Analyzes policy implications of Internet architecture (Internet protocols, domain name system, packet switching, peer-to-peer) and surveys policy issues about content, privacy, intellectual property, and governance.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive review of contemporary issues and perspectives on leadership, including multi-disciplinary and systems-oriented approaches as well as classic theory, moving to the examination of evolving contemporary beliefs.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Social Policy Issues
courses.description: A review of conceptual and analytical perspectives in social policy and coverage of major areas of persistent social problems, including health care, welfare reform, housing, education, reproductive issues, and gerontology.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3201 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Urban Policy
courses.description: Urban policy and urban economic development examined historically, nationally, and locally. Approaches to urban development and redevelopment.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level POL 1101 Minimum Grade of D

courses.description: The status of women in American society as a function of rights and opportunities conferred upon women by governmental actions and as influenced by forces of social change.

courses.title: Gender, Science, Technology, and Public Policy
courses.description: The course focuses on the connections between gender, science, and technology, and issuues of public policy.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Business and Government
courses.description: How government regulates business and markets, and how business exercises power and influence on government in areas such as antitrust, financial markets, safety and health, and environmental quality.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Public Policy
courses.description: Examination of relationships between science, technology, and government, and their mutual influence on public and private decisions.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Technology, Innovation, and Policy
courses.description: Theories and concepts of technological innovation and diffusion, economic development, and the role of public and private institutions in technological development at the firm, industry, regional, national, and international levels.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Regulation
courses.description: Examines historical, legal, economic, and political rationales for regulation. Survey of administrative law and processes, risk analysis/management, expertise and public, and current topical issues. Credit not allowed for both PUBP 4440 and PUBP 6440.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level POL 1101 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level INTA 1200 Minimum Grade of D

courses.description: An introduction to the role of information and knowledge in modern private and public organizations. It covers theoretical and practical aspects of information seeking, gathering and use in organizations as well as knowledge creation and its role in private and public management. Credit not awarded for both PUBP 4501 and PUBP 6501.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Mass Communication Policy
courses.description: Examines mass media influences, activities, characteristics, and behavior with respect to the political process and government. Structure of media markets, characteristics of news and advertising, and impacts of changing technologies on political processes.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level POL 1101 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Overview of GIS concepts, methods, and terminology, Introduction to PC-based GIS software. Applications to marketing, natural resource management, and public information systems. Students use case studies to design and implement actual projects.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Advanced GIS Topics: Spatial Analysis, GIS Programming, and Map Internet Server
courses.description: Introduction to raster-based GIS software, Avenue script language, and map Internet server. Applications to marketing, natural resource management, and public information systems.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 4530 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Senior Seminar/Thesis
courses.description: A capstone course usually taken in the student's last term before graduation, the senior seminar and thesis involves writing an original paper entailing policy analysis relevant to a public or nonprofit agency.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Legal Practice
courses.description: This course develops skills in reading and comprehension of legal materials, analysis of legal writing, and document drafting in selected areas of law.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3000 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3610 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.description: Investigation of the principal environmental laws and regulations. The class will also consider philosophical and ethical underpinnings of environmental law.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Law, Medicine, and Ethics
courses.description: This course will examine common ethical dilemmas and challenges in medicine, methods for thinking ethically, and how the law responds to these situations.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Technology Law, Policy, and Management
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of patent law and survey of other forms of intellectual property protection, including trademark, copyright, and trade secrets.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Internet Law
courses.description: Covers issues including copyright (including music/video file sharing), privacy; freedom of speech (including defamation and obscenity), jurisdiction, regulation, and crimes as applied to the Internet.

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: Public Policy Internship
courses.description: Course projects related to professional internships. Topics, credit, and requirements to be arranged by student, instructor, and sponsor.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level POL 1101 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level INTA 1200 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: PUBP
courses.title: OLA Legal Internship
courses.description: Supervised professional internship with the Georgia Tech Office of Legal Affairs.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 3610 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level PUBP 4811 Minimum Grade of D
